Good work on #372 — the class guard across 11 components × 4 render sites is exactly right, and catching that Flatten must not cap an already-short detail is a good call.

Two follow-ups on the same PR. Both are things I verified live just now, so treat them as ground truth.

## 1. Your wording deviation picked the wrong side — please switch it

You matched main's `install it with \`scripts/install.sh\` from the entire-brain checkout`. That remedy is NOT runnable for an end user: it assumes they have the entire-brain source checkout. Most users installing the plugin do not.

VERIFIED LIVE just now:
```
$ entire plugin search graph
* graph   Deterministic local code graph for symbol search, relationship tracing, and change-impact analysis [official]
* = installed. Install with 'entire plugin install <name>'.
```
`graph` is in the official plugin index and `entire plugin install graph` is the correct, runnable form. The #350 branch already uses it (`semantic.go:1250`, `:1252`, `:1324`) — it is part of the "make printed advice runnable" fix stack. main simply has not caught up.

Change `providerdetail.MissingRemedy` to the `entire plugin install graph` form. Keep your agreement test — the point is that both components agree AND the thing they agree on actually works. Note in the PR body that this intentionally diverges from main's current wording because main's is not runnable, so the reviewer sees it was deliberate.

## 2. Same PR: the version-skew remedy points at the wrong component

Separate condition, same subsystem, and it is the mirror image of the bug you just fixed — a message and its remedy disagreeing.

- `internal/cli/semantic.go:1804` says: `semantic provider emitted schema_version %q but this build reads %s; minors are additive, so the snapshot is usable, but upgrade **entire-brain** to ingest everything %q carries`
- `internal/cli/doctor.go:696` has a STATIC per-component remedy: `"semantic provider": "entire plugin install graph"`

So on a version-skew warning, doctor tells the user to install/upgrade **graph** — the side that is already ahead. Doing it cannot help, and may widen the skew.

Observed verbatim:
```
semantic provider: warn (provider=degraded (semantic provider emitted schema_version "1.3" but this build reads 1.1; minors are additive, so the snapshot is usable, but upgrade entire-b…; run `entire plugin install graph`)
```

Root cause is structural: the remedy is a static map keyed by component name, so it cannot vary by condition. Make the semantic-provider remedy condition-dependent — provider-missing → install graph; provider-ahead/version-skew → upgrade entire-brain. If other entries in that map have the same latent problem, say so in your report rather than fixing them all.

## Tests
Weakening-verify both, as before. For #2, the valuable guard is the property, not the string: **a remedy must name the component the message says is behind**. Assert that for both conditions, so the two can never disagree again.

## Constraints unchanged
Do NOT touch `internal/cli/connect_cmd.go`, `hosted_sync.go`, `hosted_placement*.go` — another agent is in `internal/cli/status_render.go` and `setup.go` right now, so if your change needs either of those, stop and report instead of editing. ## The problem

PR #340 removed a false promise from the CLI's `connect` help: that the daemon and session-end hook resolve the hosted binding automatically. The docs still make that promise.

GROUND TRUTH, verified live by me:
- `entire repo` offers ONLY: clone, create, delete, get, list, mirror, visibility.

- `entire repo whereami` does not exist either.
- `entire repo get` DOES exist but REQUIRES the repo id as an argument, so it cannot perform discovery — you must already know the answer to ask it.

# `entire brain setup` — redesign spec

## Why

The machinery is fine (`refreshProgress` phases, `liveTerminal` repaints, TTY-gated
`tui.Render`). The problem is volume and redundancy. On a TTY today:

```
⠹ ✗✓✓✓ instant core: doc index              <- 9 sub-components as a cryptic tick-run
⠹ ✗✓✓✓✓✓✓ instant core: pattern layer
✓ instant core ready in 300ms — built seed, history, docs, semantic, fact… done
  session export failed (no_egress: a complete readable local checkpoint …)
− pre-edit hook already wired (…/.claude/settings.json) skipped
− fact backfill (--no-backfill) skipped
…
  instant     ✗ session export ✓ seed baseline ✓ history index ✓ doc index …   <- ALL 9 AGAIN
```

The same nine components are rendered three times: inline in the spinner, in the
completion sentence, and again in the summary. `setup.go` is 1928 lines with 37
progress call sites.

Token spend is also opt-OUT (`--no-backfill`). A first run distills without asking.

## Target

### Seven phases, one line each while running, one line each when done

| # | phase | what it covers |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Detect** | repo, git state, agent CLI, model + effort, graph provider, hosted binding |
| 2 | **Build** | the whole instant core — 9 components behind ONE progress bar |
| 3 | **Agents** | agent instructions + pre-edit hook + session-end hook |
| 4 | **Facts** | **asks before spending**; then distills |
| 5 | **Workspace** | registration |
| 6 | **Watcher** | daemon (keep today's excellent pre-install warning verbatim) |
| 7 | **Ready** | verdict + next steps |

Sub-components report *into* their phase's bar, never as their own top-level line.
A failure promotes exactly one line beneath its phase — never a stderr dump
(that invariant is already enforced by `providerdetail.Flatten`).

### The summary block stops repeating the phases

Today it re-lists every component. It should show only what the phase lines could
not: paths (repo, brain), the verdict, and any failure's one-line reason.

### Ask before spending tokens

Phase 4 prompts when, and only when, there is something to spend on:

```
  Facts   12 sessions can be distilled into durable facts.
          Agent: claude-code · model: claude-haiku-5-5 · effort: low
          Estimated: ~12 agent calls, newest first, resumable.

          Distill now? [y/N]
```

- Default **No**. Enter = skip. Never spend on silence.
- Skipped → the brain is still fully queryable; print the one command that starts it later.
- **Non-interactive (no TTY, CI, piped) must never block**: no prompt, default No, say so in one line.
- `--yes` / `--no-backfill` keep working and suppress the prompt. `--yes` is the
  only way to spend without a human.
- Do not prompt when there is nothing to distill (0 sessions) or no agent CLI.

### Show model and provider capabilities

Phase 1 prints what was detected, so the Facts prompt is an informed decision:

```
  Detect  repo acme-payments · 13 commits · clean tree
          agent    claude-code (claude-haiku-5-5, effort low)
          provider entire-graph v0.4.1   semantic ✓  entities ✓
          hosted   not bound — local-only (COR-2029)
```

Each line states a real capability. Anything unavailable says so and names its
one-line remedy. No line that cannot be acted on.

### Colour

Per-phase accent carried by `tui.Phase`; state colour on the glyph
(running / ok / skipped / failed). Must degrade correctly for `NO_COLOR`, a
non-UTF-8 locale, and a pipe — those are four distinct cases and
`newProgressWithRenderer` already separates them. Do not hand-roll ANSI; go
through `tui.Render`.

## Non-negotiables

- `setup` still exits 0 whenever the brain is queryable; non-zero only when nothing usable exists.
- Re-running stays safe and resumes rather than restarts.
- No phase may spend a token before phase 4's consent.
- Every printed command must be runnable verbatim.
- Behaviour identical under a pipe, minus the repaints.
MD

input.message:
Extra requirement for the setupui work, with a measurement behind it.

## Terminal width is currently unhandled — make it a hard constraint

I measured today's output under a real PTY at forced widths:

```
width 40: longest rendered line = 202 chars  -> OVERFLOWS (5x)
width 60: longest rendered line = 202 chars  -> OVERFLOWS (3.4x)
```

The offender is the summary line you are already deleting:
`  instant     ✗ session export  ✓ seed baseline  ✓ history index  ✓ doc index  ✓ semantic index  ✓ pattern layer  ✓ entity index  ✓ memory coordinator  (340ms)`

It is emitted at a fixed 202 chars regardless of terminal width, so it wraps into unreadable mush on any normal split pane.

### Requirements
- NO line the new UI emits may exceed the terminal width. Detect width from the TTY; fall back to 80 when unknown (pipe, no winsize).
- Truncate or re-flow rather than wrap. If you truncate, do it on a word/segment boundary with an ellipsis, never mid-escape-sequence and never mid-multibyte-rune — `репо-名前` paths and `✓`/`⠋` glyphs are all in play (I verified unicode paths reach this code).
- The progress bar must size itself to the available width, not a constant.
- Respect `COLUMNS` when set, since that is how people test this.

### Test it for real
Add a width test that renders at **40, 60, 80 and 200 columns** and asserts no emitted line exceeds the width. Weakening-verify it: hardcode a 202-char line and confirm the test goes RED at 40 and 80.

For the PTY harness, `script` does NOT work in this environment (`tcgetattr/ioctl: Operation not supported on socket`). Use Python's `pty.fork()` plus `fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0, 0))` — that is what I used and it works. Strip ANSI with `s/\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[a-zA-Z]//g` and convert `\r` to newline before measuring, or you will measure the repaint stream rather than the rendered frame.

## Two more things I verified that you can rely on
- Interrupting setup mid-run (SIGINT) leaves no corruption; the next run recovers cleanly. Don't add recovery scaffolding for a problem that doesn't exist.
- Two concurrent `setup` runs both exit 0 with no lock error. Your UI must not assume it is the only writer, but it also need not serialise anything.

Everything else in the original brief stands, including the file boundary — still do not touch `setup.go`, `status_render.go`, `semantic.go`, `doctor.go`, `connect_cmd.go`, `hosted_*`.

Two corrections and one concrete design target. All measured, all after fixing a flaw in my own sandbox.

## Correction: ignore any "degraded" you saw in my earlier material

My sandbox set `ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY=1` as a safety rail, and that alone makes session export refuse (`no_egress: ...`), turning every run into "Brain ready (degraded)". Same repo, same binary, rail removed: all nine components build and it reports plain `Brain ready`. The rail manufactured the symptom. `~/devenv/brain-demo/env.sh` no longer sets it.

Corrected baseline for the healthy path: **33 lines**, verdict `Brain ready`.

## The design target — 47 lines vs 2, same program

This contrast is the whole brief in one pair of numbers.

A repo with **no commits yet**:
- **47 lines**, three component failures (seed baseline, semantic index, entity index), verdict `Brain set up, but not queryable`.

A directory that is **not a git repo at all**:
```
not a git repository: /path/to/notgit
entire-brain setup builds every source it has -- sessions, seed, docs, semantic
index, entities -- from git history, so it needs git and a repository.
run `git init` here and make at least one commit, or name a repository:
entire-brain setup <path>
```
- **2 lines** (plus wrap). What is wrong, why it matters, two runnable ways out. Exit 1.

Same class of problem — "this repo has nothing to index yet" — and 23x the output for the easier case. The no-commits path should read much closer to the second: state the condition once, name the one action, stop. It should NOT render three red component failures, because nothing is broken.

**Make this a test case.** A repo with zero commits must produce a short, single-reason result, not a failure list. Assert a line-count ceiling for it (pick a defensible number and justify it) and weakening-verify by restoring the per-component failure rendering.

More generally: a phase whose inputs do not exist yet is **not** a failure. Expected-empty and broken must render differently — that distinction is the core of the redesign, and PR #373 (now open) establishes it for the sessions component specifically. Read that diff if it helps; do not duplicate it.

## Corrected edge-case baseline you can design against

| case | exit | lines | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| empty repo, no commits | 0 | 47 | Brain set up, but not queryable |
| not a git repo | 1 | 2 | (exemplary) |
| dirty worktree | 0 | 41 | Brain set up, but not queryable |
| detached HEAD / binary-only / spaces / unicode / read-only | 0 | 32-33 | Brain ready |

No crashes or hangs anywhere, including unicode paths (`репо-名前`) and paths with spaces, so handle those as working input rather than hazards.

Everything else in the brief stands, including the file boundary. `setup.go` is now free — but it is MINE to wire; keep building standalone packages.

The width test couldn't see it because it measures after stripping escapes; the length was fine, the cut position wasn't. `TruncateTo` now measures visible cells, never cuts inside a sequence, and closes a colour it cuts through. A PTY capture carried **3 partial sequences before, 0 after** — and I ran the detector against the pre-fix capture first, so that zero means something.

My own first fix was also wrong, and the tests caught it in one run: `[` is `0x5B`, which sits inside the CSI final-byte range, so my scanner stopped at the bracket and read `38;5;45m` as visible text. The parameters have to be skipped first.

`n` → nothing starts (stub log shows one `--version` call, so declining spends nothing). `y` → backfill starts. Piped stdin → *"no terminal to ask, and silence is not consent"*, no block, no spend.

**Two real bugs I found by running it rather than reading it.**

The live bar was truncating **mid-ANSI-escape** — `\x1b[3` with no final byte, which makes a terminal swallow the next characters. The width test couldn't see it because it measures after stripping escapes. Negative control: **3 partial sequences before the fix, 0 after**. My own first fix was wrong too — `[` is `0x5B`, inside the CSI final-byte range, so my scanner stopped at the bracket; the tests caught it in one run.

And a truth-telling wart of exactly the kind this whole effort is about: a bare re-run said `not distilled (--no-backfill)` to someone who typed no such flag. `resolveSetupToggle` folds "typed" and "remembered" into one boolean, so the message blamed a flag that was never passed and never mentioned `--backfill`, the only way back. It now says *"you declined on an earlier run; --backfill starts it"*.

Three corrections from this round, two of them about my own work.

**I collided with my own subagent.** I handed it the `brain-350-stack` worktree and then committed, pushed and rebuilt the demo binary inside it while it worked. It reported "an unattended agent with push rights on this branch" — that was me. The changes were additive so nothing was lost, but it's a real process failure and it's on the board.

**My provenance test was under-guarded, and the agent caught it.** `f59a1829` tested only the renderer, so wiring the field to a constant `false` kept the suite green. It added the whole-run guard. I then applied that lesson to the matching defect it had flagged but left — `--no-daemon` had the identical bug — and this time weakened **both** directions:

```
- Facts     not distilled (you declined on an earlier run; --backfill starts it)
- Watcher   background watcher (you declined on an earlier run; --daemon installs it)
```

Neither line now credits a flag you didn't type, and both name the way back.

**The `git log` hiding claim doesn't reproduce** — `rev-list --count`, `--oneline` and `--format=%H` all agree at 17, so my audit path was sound. But that's now the *second* intermittent output-loss incident in this shell (the first was `grep -c` returning 0 for six real matches). I've written it into memory as a property of the environment: any audit whose answer is a count or an absence gets its evidence and denominator printed, and gets re-run.

Two things the agent asks you to confirm, and I agree they're yours:

**The exit-code change.** When semantic, seed and history all fail, #350 exited 0 ("a brain with captured sessions is worth keeping"); it now exits non-zero because `setup && query` was proceeding on a brain that cannot answer. That was my instruction, and it's a behaviour change to a shipped contract.

I fixed the scaling defect — the one item on the hook's list that was actually mine. **`docs/release-notes` @ `7bd7f102`**, full suite green.

`selectRoutedCheckpointSessions` was issuing one `entire checkpoint explain --json` subprocess per checkpoint, serially, at the 0.97/sec I measured. brain setup --no-backfill --no-daemon - why this

Fair challenge — those flags make the demo *less* representative, and you should know what they're hiding.

**Why they're there:** `--no-backfill` because backfill defaults to **on**, so a bare `brain setup` with an agent on PATH distills immediately and spends real money. `--no-daemon` because setup otherwise installs a persistent launchd watcher that restarts at every login.

**What they cost you:** two of the seven phases don't do their real thing. You see `- Facts  not distilled (--no-backfill)` and `- Watcher  background watcher (--no-daemon)` — the skip lines, not the behaviour. And Facts is where the consent prompt lives, which is the thing you actually asked for.

**To see the full seven phases for real, safely:**

```bash
source ~/devenv/brain-demo/env.sh
export PATH="$BRAIN_DEMO_ROOT/fakebin:$PATH"   # stub agent — 'y' cannot reach a real model
cd "$BRAIN_DEMO_ROOT/with-sessions"            # has 268 real sessions
brain setup --backfill-budget 1
```

That runs **all seven**: Facts actually prompts you `Distill now? [y/N]`, and Watcher actually installs — into the sandbox, under a scoped launchd label (`io.entire.brain-watch.*.10affb60`), not your real one at pid 5190. Remove it after with `brain setup --uninstall-daemon`.

Drop the `fakebin` line and answering `y` spends real tokens. That's the only difference between the safe version and the live one.

That's the fifth vacuous guard I've caught in this session, and the only thing that exposed it was looking at an actual video frame. Reverted — a wrapper that can't change a pixel, plus a test that certifies it, is worse than neither.

A three-product interaction bug, found 2026-10-15 by running `entire brain
setup` against the REAL `devenv/cli` checkout. Root-caused by instrumenting
entire-graph after four wrong hypotheses.

**The chain:**
1. Entire CLI writes a promisor remote (`blob:none`) for the checkpoint remote
   when `filtered_fetches: true` — the default where a checkpoint remote exists.
2. entire-graph's `gitMetadataSafeForSubprocess` refuses ALL git subprocesses on
   a repo whose config declares a promisor remote.
3. That flips `useCache=false`, and `commit`/`tree` are resolved only inside
   that branch, so the snapshot header ships EMPTY with `warnings: 0`.
4. entire-brain's `validateLiveSemanticHeader` correctly refuses it:
   `semantic snapshot header missing commit`.
5. setup loses its semantic index, with a message naming neither cause nor cure.

**It also silently drops records:** 191,681 with the promisor vs 191,904
without, and is ~26% slower (cache disabled).

**Invisible in testing:** repos with no checkpoint remote are fine, and
`git clone --local` does not copy the config — so a CLONE indexes fine while
the real checkout does not.

**Verified workaround** (cost: loses blobless checkpoint fetches):
unset BOTH `remote.<ckpt>.promisor` AND `remote.<ckpt>.partialclonefilter`.
Unsetting promisor alone is NOT enough.

Full writeup with repro and three candidate fixes:
`~/devenv/brain-demo/ISSUE-graph-promisor.md`. Belongs to entire-graph; the
actionable defect is the SILENCE, not the refusal.

Fresh recon done. Two findings change the plan before I give you the order.

## Finding 1 — merging was never blocked on approval

I re-read the actual branch protection instead of trusting the earlier refusal:

```
requiredApprovingReviewCount: 0      ← nobody has to approve
requiresConversationResolution: true ← but 0 unresolved threads on 341/372/373/374/350
enforce_admins: true                 ← so --admin would NOT have worked anyway
mergeQueue: null
required checks: 18 named contexts — "Entire Gates" is NOT one of them
```

I diffed the 18 required contexts against each PR's rollup: **zero required checks missing on #341, #372, #373.** `mergeStateStatus: UNSTABLE` = a *non-required* check (Entire Gates) is red, which does not block. The earlier "base branch policy prohibits the merge" was a transient — checks hadn't landed yet at that moment.

**So the only input needed is your word. Not a reviewer.**

## Finding 2 — the Linear board cannot drive this work

| | |
|---|---|
| Open PRs on entire-brain | **29** |
| …carrying a `COR-` id | **7** |
| …with no Linear issue at all | **22** |
| M1 issues | 1 (COR-2007) |
| **M2 / M3 / M4 issues** | **0 / 0 / 0** |
| M5 remaining | 1 (COR-2002) |
| Post launch | 18 |

M2 "Close the brain blockers", M3 "GA the MCP surface", M4 "brain-bench eval gate" have descriptions and target dates and **not one ticket between them**. "Go on Linear issues" today means working 2 tickets while 29 PRs rot. Phase 0 below fixes that first.

## Finding 3 — main moved under the stack

Dependabot merges + #387 landed. **10 of 29 PRs are now CONFLICTING**, including #350, #374, #351, #352. #350 is 130 commits ahead of its base and behind main.

And the summary's claim that #350 carries #372/#373/#374 is **half right**: `internal/setupui` and `internal/providerdetail` are in #350's tree, but the files have **diverged** — `providerdetail.go`, `semantic.go`, `setup.go`, `setup_invocation.go` all differ between #350 and #372's head. #374 has one commit #350 never absorbed (`474462b2` LF pinning).

---

# The order

**Phase 0 — make the board real** *(no code, ~30 min, no approval needed)*
Group the 22 orphan PRs into ~6 themed issues under M2 and attach the PRs; file the entire-graph promisor bug under M1 (I searched — no issue exists); flag M3/M4 for your decision. Without this, every later phase is untrackable.

**Phase 1 — stop the bleed** *(no approval needed)*
Refresh the 10 CONFLICTING branches against main. Every day main moves this gets worse.

**Phase 2 — land the stack** ⚠️ *needs your GO*
Recommendation: make **#350 the true superset** — merge main in, then fold #341, #372, #373, #374's leftover commit into it, resolve the divergence **once**, run the full suite **once**, land as a single merge. Alternative is ~8 sequential merges with ~8 conflict resolutions and ~8 suite runs. I'd produce a reconciliation report naming every file where #350 and #372/#374 disagreed and which side won, so the big merge is auditable.
Then the independents: **#367 and #368 first** — they're the only two PRs with *zero* failing checks, so they're the cheapest proof that merging works. Then #388/#389/#390 (the COR-2111/2116/2126/2143 set). #365 (BM25 retrieval swap) gets its own review + bench, not folded in.

**Phase 3 — M1, the real GA blocker**
COR-2007: brain pins semantic schema 1.1, graph emits 1.3 → brain refuses graph's index. Shipping v0.2.0 without this means outsiders get a brain that rejects the graph it's supposed to read. **Must land before any release.**

**Phase 4 — M5 COR-2002**, local dev loop.

**Phase 5 — release** ⚠️ *needs your GO + a version number*
Delete the local-only stray tags first (`v0.2.0`/`v0.3.0`/`v0.3.1` — `release.yml` fires on `push: tags: v*`, so one careless `--tags` publishes from whatever they point at), cut stable, then clean-room outsider install confirming the new version **and** the `[y/N]` consent gate.

**Phase 6 — M2/M3/M4 decision**: populate or move out of P0.

---

Phases 0 and 1 need nothing from you and unblock everything else — **say go and I'll start there** while you decide on Phase 2. The three inputs I still need: **merge go-ahead**, a **version number**, and **yes/no on deleting the stray tags**.

Phases 0–6 (Linear reconciliation, rebasing 10 conflicting PRs, landing the stack, COR-2007 schema fix, COR-2002, release v0.2.0, and the clean-room install check) have not been carried out. content.text: Themes are clean. Creating the M1 issues first — the promisor defect has no ticket anywhere:

input.title: entire-graph: a promisor remote makes the semantic snapshot identity-less, and Brain correctly refuses it
input.description:
Root-caused 2026-10, no ticket existed. This is an **entire-graph** defect that presents as a Brain failure, which is why it has been invisible.

## Symptom

`entire graph` emits a snapshot whose `commit` and `tree` are **empty strings**, with `warnings: 0` — it reports success. Brain then refuses it:

```
semantic snapshot header missing commit
```

Brain is right to refuse. The same run also **silently drops 223 records** and is **~26% slower**.

## Chain

1. Entire CLI writes `filtered_fetches: true`, which creates a **promisor remote** (`blob:none`) for the checkpoint remote.
2. `gitMetadataSafeForSubprocess` sees the promisor config and refuses **all** git subprocesses — a blanket safety check, not a targeted one.
3. With no git subprocess, `useCache=false`.
4. Snapshot identity (`commit`/`tree`) is never resolved, and nothing warns.

The failure is silent at every hop. Four plausible hypotheses were disproved by measurement before instrumentation found this.

## Verified workaround

Unset **both**:

```
git config --unset remote.<ckpt>.promisor
git config --unset remote.<ckpt>.partialclonefilter
```

Unsetting `promisor` alone is **not sufficient** — this was tested. Cost of the workaround: you lose blobless checkpoint fetches.

## Why this is M1

M1 is "version-stamp entire-sem and freeze the schema so everything downstream can trust the contract." A snapshot that reports success with no identity breaks that contract at the source. Any consumer that trusts `warnings: 0` is reading a snapshot it cannot anchor.

## Fix direction

`gitMetadataSafeForSubprocess` should not be all-or-nothing. Failing that, identity resolution must emit a warning and a non-success status rather than an empty header.

Full write-up with the disproved hypotheses and the instrumentation: `~/devenv/brain-demo/ISSUE-graph-promisor.md`

content.text: COR-2146 filed. Now the rest of the board — batching:

input.title: Generated agent guides must use commands the released Graph actually has
input.description:
Brain generates the Graph/Brain agent guide that every coding agent reads. It emitted a command spelling that the **released** Graph (v0.4.0) does not have, so a user installing both from release got guidance that fails on the first query.

Fixed by using `entire graph search` in the generated normal and strict guides; current Graph keeps `search` as a compatibility alias.

**PR:** https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/368 (green, 0 failing checks, mergeable)
Fixes entire-brain#323.

## Why M1

M1 freezes the entire-sem contract. The generated guide *is* a consumer of that contract, and it was written against unreleased spellings. The durable fix is that guide generation is pinned to the oldest Graph we support, not to main.

input.title: First run tells the truth: a healthy new repo must not report itself broken
input.description:
M2 is "ship the local brain with honest claims, no overreach." This is the largest violation of it: on a **brand-new repository with a clean working tree and no finished agent session**, Brain reports a failure, recommends a command that cannot clear it, and re-emits the same failure forever.

Measured: a zero-commit repo produced **58 lines of output and exit 1** for a condition that is normal.

## PRs

| PR | What it fixes | State |
|---|---|---|
| [#373](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/373) | A repo with no captured sessions is not broken | mergeable |
| [#345](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/345) | `setup` and `status` say what is actually true on a first run | **CONFLICTING** |
| [#321](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/321) | Distill timeout configurable; the nested-repo trap is named rather than silent | **CONFLICTING** |

Both traps in #321 came from a real install report, and both failed silently — which is what made them expensive.

## Done when

A fresh repo, a repo with no sessions, and a nested repo each produce output a first-time user can act on, and the exit code reflects whether the brain is queryable rather than whether every optional component ran.

input.title: Setup wires the brain in, asks before spending tokens, and remembers a decline
input.description:
Two gaps between "setup exited 0" and "the user has a working brain".

**It wasn't discoverable.** Setup did not wire the brain into the agents on the machine, so a successful install produced a brain no agent would ever call.

**It spent money without asking.** Distillation runs a model. There was no consent gate.

## PRs

| PR | What it does | State |
|---|---|---|
| [#342](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/342) | Make the brain discoverable to agents; remember what the user declined | mergeable |
| [#374](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/374) | Seven-phase progress UI, capability block, `[y/N]` distill consent | **CONFLICTING** |

#374 measured: healthy run **46 → 14 lines**, zero-commit repo **58 → 9**, graph-missing **225 → 18**. Consent defaults to **No**, never reads stdin without a TTY, and `--yes` / `--backfill` / `--no-backfill` override it. Four render modes (colour, NO_COLOR, non-UTF-8 ASCII, pipe), width-safe at 40/60/80/200.

A remembered decline now names the flag that reverses it ("you declined on an earlier run; `--backfill`/`--daemon` …") instead of blaming a flag the user never passed.

## Note

`internal/setupui` exists in #350's tree but **diverged** from #374's head — #374 carries one commit #350 never absorbed (`474462b2`, LF golden pinning). Reconcile before landing either.

input.title: Everything Brain prints must be something the reader can actually run
input.description:
A five-PR class, all the same defect: Brain printed text that looked like advice but could not be acted on — wrong dispatch spelling, a command that doesn't exist, a remedy with no escape hatch, or a raw dump of another tool's `--help`.

Worst measured case: on a machine without the entire-graph plugin, `entire-brain setup` printed **168 lines, 116 of them the host CLI's `--help` screen, dumped twice**.

## PRs

| PR | What it fixes | State |
|---|---|---|
| [#372](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/372) | Summarise the provider failure instead of dumping the host CLI's help | mergeable |
| [#341](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/341) | `doctor` prints only what a reader can act on | mergeable |
| [#347](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/347) | Printed advice is runnable, and names the escape hatch | mergeable |
| [#348](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/348) | Remedies render in the reader's dispatch spelling | mergeable |
| [#349](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/349) | Three remedies the reader could not follow | mergeable |

## Supporting work already done

- `providerdetail.Summary` elides from the **middle**, so a Go error's trailing cause survives truncation.
- ANSI-aware `TruncateTo` in `internal/tui` — truncation was cutting inside an escape sequence (`\x1b[3…`). Negative control: 3 partial escapes before, 0 after.
- `setupui.FlattenText` carries the same fix (third site in the class).
- `truncateDoctorDetail` was investigated and **deliberately left alone** — it is designed to end on a whole runnable command, and a test caught the attempted change.

## Done when

No Brain output contains another tool's help screen, and every printed command runs as spelled in the reader's own dispatch.

input.title: Entire's own files must not make Entire's own install gate refuse
input.description:
The install gate treats a dirty working tree as a refusal condition, but **Entire's own installers write into the tree** — so installing Entire could put the repo into a state where installing Entire is blocked. Self-inflicted and confusing.

Same PR also stops the setup silently picking Codex when it should not.

**PR:** [#346](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/346) — mergeable

## Done when

A clean checkout plus a completed Entire install still passes the gate, and no agent is selected without the user seeing which one.

input.title: A failed memory prepass must record why, and stop retrying what cannot change
input.description:
A failed prepass left no reason behind and was retried on every subsequent run, including when the cause was permanent. The user saw repeated unexplained failure and paid for the retries.

**PR:** [#343](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/343) — mergeable

## Done when

Every prepass failure records its cause, and a cause that cannot change on a retry is not retried.

input.title: Retrieval returns output an agent can accept, and discloses what was dropped
input.description:
Bottom of a three-PR stack — nothing above it matters if the tools error or silently lie about completeness.

Two problems: the tools returned output an agent could not accept, and when results were dropped (truncation, caps) the response did not say so, which makes a partial answer indistinguishable from a complete one.

**PR:** [#329](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/329) — **CONFLICTING**, needs refresh against main

## Done when

Every retrieval response is accepted by the agent that called it, and any dropped rows are disclosed in the response itself rather than inferred.

input.title: Replace facts semantic retrieval (bundled embedder + RRF) with in-process BM25 + taxonomy filters
input.description:
Drops the bundled embedder and RRF fusion for facts retrieval in favour of in-process BM25 plus taxonomy filters.

**PR:** [#365](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/365) — mergeable, Entire Gates red

## This one does not ride the fix stack

Every other M2 PR is a truth-in-output fix with no behavioural risk. This changes **what facts come back**, so it needs its own review and its own measurement, and must not be folded into the integration branch.

Required before landing:
- A retrieval quality comparison against the current ranker on a fixed query set, reported with the median beside the mean.

input.title: Brain's Git reads must not lock the user's shared index
input.description:
Brain's read-only Git subprocesses refreshed and **locked the shared index**, so a background brief could block the user's own `git` commands in the same repo.

Fix: pass `--no-optional-locks`, and use `git diff-index --shortstat HEAD` for the brief's diff summary to avoid the remaining `git diff` index refresh. Both invocations and the resulting diff stat are pinned in regression tests.

**PR:** [#367](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/367) — mergeable, **0 failing checks**

## Known limit worth encoding in the test

`--no-optional-locks` stops `git status` but **not** `git diff <commit>`. If a future read needs that form, the durable fix is `GIT_INDEX_FILE` pointed at a copy, which keeps both the answer and the lock-freedom.

content.text: #388/#389/#390 map to **P1**, not P0 — correctly tracked already. But that surfaced a problem:
COR-2002 is exactly #351 + #352, and I already have both root causes. Posting them:

input.body:
Both local-only failures in this ticket are now root-caused, and two PRs are open against them.

## 1. The envelope-limit test failure — root cause found, PR open

It is **not** load flakiness. The test's bound sat **inside the fake server's own cap**, so it was measuring the test harness's scheduling rather than the client's envelope. Measured **3 of 6 red on main** at `GOMAXPROCS=1`, which is why it reproduces locally and not on CI runners with more cores.

**PR:** [#351](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/351) — bounds the guard by the client, not the writer. Currently **CONFLICTING** against main.

## 2. The `internal/cli` package timeout — root cause found, PR open

`internal/cli` under `-race` runs **17–20 minutes against a 20-minute cap**. The deadline was set inside the suite's own runtime, so it is a coin flip, not a failure. A red `test (macos-latest)` on this repo is usually the cap, not the diff under review.

**PR:** [#352](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/352) — gives the suite a deadline above its own runtime plus a real backstop. Currently **CONFLICTING** against main.

## 3. A third local-only divergence this ticket does not yet name

Shells that export **`FORCE_COLOR`** make colour-asserting tests fail locally on correct code. If `FORCE_COLOR` is set (ours is `3`), those tests fail on a clean checkout of main. Worth adding to the "required local setup" answer for outcome 1, because it produces exactly the symptom in this ticket — local red, CI green, same commit.

The matching discipline for running these locally at all: `GOMAXPROCS=1 -p 1 -parallel 1`. A local full suite saturates the machine (measured 11 cores) and then the timeouts above fire for reasons that have nothing to do with the code.

## Suggested close condition

Outcome 1 is answered by landing #351 and #352 and documenting `FORCE_COLOR` + the `GOMAXPROCS` discipline. Outcome 2 (settle `CONTRIBUTING.md` pre-push guidance) is still open and is the only part needing a decision rather than a merge.

input.title: Cut a stable entire-brain release and re-run the outsider install against it
input.description:
M5's exit criterion is "someone outside the team can install and run it." The **mechanism** is met and the **content** is not — this issue closes the gap, and closes M5.

## Verified current state

- `entireio/entire-brain` and `entireio/entire-graph` are both **public**.
- `curl -fsSL .../scripts/get-brain.sh | bash` from a clean directory returns **exit 0** with checksum verification and a working binary.
- entire-brain's only stable tag is **v0.1.0 (2026-09-20)**. entire-graph is on v0.4.0.
- An outsider installing today gets a binary **356 commits / 46 merged PRs behind main**, with no distill consent gate.

## Blocked on

1. The M2 fix stack landing (COR-2148, COR-2149, COR-2150, COR-2151, COR-2152, COR-2155, COR-2156).
2. **COR-2007** — Brain pins semantic schema 1.1 while Graph emits 1.3. Releasing without it ships a brain that refuses the graph it is meant to read. Hard blocker.
3. A version number, from the user.

## ⚠️ Hazard to clear before tagging

Tags **`v0.2.0`, `v0.3.0`, `v0.3.1` exist as local-only tags and were never pushed**. `release.yml` fires on `push: tags: v*`, so a single stray `git push --tags` publishes a release from whatever those tags point at. Delete them locally before any release work.

## ⚠️ Scope check before tagging

The integration branch #350 contains **[#340](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/340)**, which is entirely hosted/connect code (`connect_cmd.go`, `hosted_placement.go`, `hosted_sync.go` — 369 insertions). That is **P1 · Shared / Hosted Brain** work riding inside the P0 release. Decide deliberately whether it ships in the P0 tag rather than discovering it in the changelog.

## Done when

A clean-room install on a machine with no Entire state installs the new stable version, reports that version, and shows the `[y/N]` distill consent gate before spending anything.

h2_new = """\t// What this counts is what the SERVER WROTE, which runs ahead of what the
\t// client read by however much the connection will buffer. The tolerance
\t// used to be 4MiB while the handler stopped at 8MiB, so the assertion sat
\t// INSIDE the server's own bound: it was measuring goroutine scheduling, and
\t// it failed on main at 38797312 bytes with nothing wrong with the client.
\t//
\t// The handler now offers far more than any correct client would take, and
\t// the bound is set above the buffering overshoot but far below the offer.
\t// A client that follows the stream still fails; one that stops at the
\t// ceiling passes regardless of how far the writer ran ahead. Kernel socket
\t// buffers on both ends keep accepting writes after the client stops, and
\t// tuned hosts buffer several MiB, so the tolerance only has to separate
\t// "stopped at the ceiling" from "followed the stream to the full offer".

\t\tt.Fatalf("served %d bytes, must stop near the %d ceiling rather than following the stream",
"""

## Fixed locally and verified. The ticket's premise was wrong, which changes the priority.

**Brain never refused 1.3.** `validateSemanticSchema` refuses an unknown *major* and accepts every *minor* within major 1 (ADR 0001's tolerant-reader rule). Proven by probe:

```
1.3 ACCEPTED by validateSemanticSchema
warning code=provider_schema_newer_minor severity=warning
2.0 correctly refused: unsupported semantic schema major version "2"
```

So this was **not** a release blocker, and my earlier characterisation of it as one was wrong. What actually happened: every index against a current entire-graph raised `provider_schema_newer_minor` and told the user additive facts "may not have been ingested" — **false for both additive minors.**

### What the two minors actually added, and whether Brain reads them

| Minor | Added | Already consumed? |
|---|---|---|
| **1.2** (`a636c8fd`) | `identity_revision` | **Yes.** `internal/entityindex` keys every stored delta by it and re-migrates when it changes (`build.go:251, 289, 333`) |
| **1.3** (`1ce3bbf5`) | `completeness.health` | **Yes.** Carried verbatim as the `Completeness` raw message, persisted on the manifest (`semantic.go:838`) |
| **1.3** | partial-failure `language` | **No — genuinely dropped** |

### The one real defect

Graph's `PartialFailure` carries `language`; Brain's `semanticWarning` had no such field. The provider sets it when a source fails **before any file record exists** — which is exactly when `file_path` is empty. So the one case the field exists for was the one case Brain could attribute to nothing at all.

This is the same class as the existing `file_path` / `effect_on_semantic_completeness` aliasing already documented on that type's `UnmarshalJSON`.

### Change

1. `semanticWarning.Language` added.
2. `semanticSchemaVersion` 1.1 → 1.3 — **after** the field, not before. The constant is documented as "the newest provider schema this build knows how to ingest **in full**", so bumping it first would have made that comment a lie and converted a true warning into a silent drop.

### Verification

- Full `internal/cli` suite green (174s), `internal/entityindex` green, `go vet` clean.
- **Both guards proven live by weakening:** restoring the constant to 1.1 → fails on schema 1.2 warning; breaking the `language` json tag → fails with `language dropped: got ""`.
- New tests also pin that a genuinely newer minor (1.4, 1.17) **still warns**, and that major 2.0 is **still refused** — bumping the constant must not disarm the mechanism.

Committed locally on `cor-2007-schema-13`. **Not pushed, no PR** — holding per your instruction.

## Correction: entire-graph is NOT silent. I filed this issue on a misread, and the real defect is in Brain.

Reproduced today against **entire-graph v0.4.1-nightly** in a scratch repo with `remote.ckpt.promisor=true` and `remote.ckpt.partialclonefilter=blob:none`.

### What I reported

Header: `commit: ''`, `tree: ''`, **`warnings: 0`** — "silent at every hop."

That reproduces exactly. **But it is only the first NDJSON line.** The snapshot's aggregate metadata lives on the **authoritative trailing `summary` record**, and there it says:

```
record_types: ['<header>', 'file', 'symbol', 'relation', 'summary']
SUMMARY warnings: 2
  - W_GIT_WORKTREE_FALLBACK
  - E_NO_GIT_HEAD
    detail: ... its Git config declares a promisor remote (a partial clone), so
    Git commands here can fetch objects over the network; indexing falls back to
    a filesystem walk to stay offline
```

entire-graph names the cause **and** the remedy. The "silence" was me reading line 1 — the exact trap Brain's own `semanticHeader` comment documents ("Aggregate metadata carried by the authoritative trailing summary record").

### Also wrong: "fix `gitMetadataSafeForSubprocess`"

That refusal is **correct and deliberate**. A promisor remote means git subprocesses can fetch over the network, and entire-graph's contract is no-egress (`AGENTS.md`: "never add remote fetches"). Removing or narrowing it would break that guarantee. My proposed fix direction would have been a security regression.

### The real defect, and it is ours

`validateLiveSemanticHeader` (`internal/cli/semantic.go`) returned a bare:

```
semantic snapshot header missing commit
```

`mergeSemanticSummary` runs at semantic.go:717, validation at :730 — so `header.Warnings` **already held E_NO_GIT_HEAD** when we refused. We discarded the one sentence that tells the reader what to do. That is what cost four wrong hypotheses and an instrumented bisect: not missing information, discarded information.

### Fixed

Refusals now carry the provider's own explanation, preferring `E_NO_GIT_HEAD` (names the cause) over `W_GIT_WORKTREE_FALLBACK` (restates the symptom). A provider that said nothing still gets a bare message — no empty trailer.

**Verification:** full `internal/cli` green (188s), vet clean. Two weakenings proven red — restoring the bare error fails on the dropped explanation; disabling the E_NO_GIT_HEAD preference fails on preferring the symptom. The test pins the verbatim detail strings from the live reproduction.

### Remaining, genuinely in entire-graph (small)

With git refused and no identity resolved, the summary still reports `completeness.health.status: ok`. Arguably it should not claim `ok` for a snapshot that silently has no git identity. Worth a separate, much smaller ticket against entire-graph — **not** a change to the no-egress refusal.

Committed locally on `cor-2007-schema-13`. Not pushed, no PR.

Retitling suggestion: this issue is now *"Brain discards the provider's reason for an identity-less snapshot"*, and should move from M1 to M2.

content.text: 38 MCP tools in one 2,909-line file. Enough to scope both milestones concretely. Creating the M3 issues:

input.title: Decide which of the 38 MCP tools are GA surface, and hide the rest
input.description:
M3 had no issues. This is the first of two scoping it from the actual surface.

## Measured today

`internal/cli/mcp.go` declares **38 tools** in **2,909 lines**.

38 is a lot of choices to put in front of an agent. Tool-selection quality degrades as the surface grows, and an outsider's first `brain` session sees all of them at once with no indication which are the load-bearing three (`brain_brief`, `brain_search`, `brain_status`) and which are developer or diagnostic surface.

## Precedent in this repo

COR-2001 did exactly this for the **CLI** — hid developer-only commands and grouped operator commands in `--help` — and is Done. The MCP surface never got the same treatment, so the two front doors disagree about what Brain is.

## Scope

1. Classify all 38: GA, operator/diagnostic, developer-only.
2. Hide or gate everything that is not GA, matching COR-2001's CLI classification so the two surfaces agree.
3. Pin the GA list in a test, so adding a tool is a deliberate act rather than a side effect.

## Done when

A fresh MCP client lists only the GA set, the classification matches the CLI's, and a test fails if an unclassified tool is added.

## Related

COR-2006 ("Simplify Brain's default setup and commands", Post launch) overlaps in intent — settle whether that absorbs this or follows it.

input.title: Prove the MCP surface works in both hosts, not just the one we develop in
input.description:
M3 is "harden the local MCP tool surface for the **Claude Code and Codex** plugins." Nothing currently proves the Codex half.

## Why this is not theoretical

Three recorded failures in this class, all silent, all found by accident rather than by CI:

- **`claude --safe-mode` strips every MCP server.** The only reliable check was asking the model what tools it had. A test that assumes the server is attached would pass while the surface was absent.
- **`CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS` is a single path, not comma-separated.** A comma silently breaks every plugin listed.
- **Plugin paths rot.** `CONNECTION_CLOSED` reads as a server bug but is usually a plugin pointing at a purged directory. Live example found today: this machine's `entire-brain` plugin symlink points into a `/tmp` scratchpad.

Each is a *configuration* failure that makes the tools vanish without an error the user can connect to a cause — exactly what GA cannot ship with.

## Scope

1. A smoke check per host (Claude Code, Codex) that asserts the GA tool list is actually reachable, not merely declared.
2. Assert it against a **durable** install path, and fail loudly when the resolved plugin binary lives somewhere ephemeral.
3. Make the failure name the cause — "plugin path does not exist" beats `CONNECTION_CLOSED`.

## Done when

Both hosts are exercised in CI or by a documented one-command check, and a deliberately broken plugin path produces a message naming the path.

Depends on COR-2158 fixing the GA list first — there is no point asserting a surface that is still being decided.

content.text: Now M4 — the two jobs named "benchmark" don't do what the milestone claims:

input.title: CI has two required "benchmark" jobs and neither is a regression floor
input.description:
M4 is "make brain-bench a required regression floor in CI." Two jobs on `main` are named as if they do this. **Neither does.** Read today from `.github/workflows/test.yml` and the branch-protection contexts.

Both **are** required checks:

```
benchmark-corpus
benchmark-real-components
```

But what they run is:

**`benchmark-corpus`**
```
python3 benchmarks/agent-brain/mined-scale/check_manifest.py
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s benchmarks/memory-ladder -p 'test_*.py'
python3 -B tools/coverage/python_run.py ...
```

**`benchmark-real-components`**
```
go build ./cmd/entire-brain ; go build ./cmd/entire-graph
python3 -B benchmarks/agent-brain/test_full_brain_integration.py -v
```

These are **harness unit tests plus an integration smoke test**. They prove the benchmark code runs. They do not score the brain, and nothing fails when retrieval quality regresses.

This is the dangerous shape: the board reads as covered, the branch protection reads as covered, and a quality regression lands green.

## Scope

1. Define the floor: which metric, measured on which fixed set, at what threshold.
2. Decide the estimator **before** seeing numbers, and report a bootstrap CI and the median beside the mean.
3. Wire it as a distinct required check with a name that says what it gates — not a third job called "benchmark".

## Preconditions that are not optional

- **Power.** A floor that cannot detect the regression it exists to catch is theatre. The recorded MDE at n=30 is ~25 points; a threshold tighter than the suite can resolve will fire on noise.
- **Run-level variance.** Measured ~87% of paired variance is run-level, and the same instance run twice correlates r=−0.022. The floor must be paired on identical instances and must never be satisfied by replicating instances.
- **Blocked on COR-2160.** The harness is not currently trustworthy enough to gate merges on.

input.title: Land the BrainMark harness fixes before anything is gated on its scores
input.description:
A regression floor is only as trustworthy as the harness producing the number. BrainMark currently is not, and this must land before COR-2160 can gate merges.

## The 2026-08-29 harness audit found 9 defects, 3 of them disqualifying

- **The arm is named in the packet.** The thing under test can see which arm it is. Any result from a run with this property is uninterpretable.
- **5 of 6 ungradable arms rendered as `resolved:0`.** A run that could not be graded was reported as a clean zero — indistinguishable from a real failure, and it silently drags the mean.
- **The gold patch was on `PATH`.** The answer was reachable from inside the run.

PRs **#166–#174**, which carry the fixes and are unmerged.

input.title: A component stays "failed" after the cause is gone, and two status surfaces disagree about it
input.description:
Found live on a developer machine, 2026-10-16, against the installed brain (v0.1.0) for `gh/entirehq/devenv`.

## Observed

`brain_status` reports the `patterns` component as:

```
"name": "patterns", "state": "failed",
"detail": "parse brain manifest: memory_state_corrupt: brain manifest cannot be
           parsed: json: unknown field \"suppressed_warnings\""
```

`brain_patterns_status`, called seconds later, reports:

```
"present": true, "freshness": "current"
```

with `last_run.at = 2026-10-11T22:58:10Z` and every counter zero.

**Two tools, opposite verdicts, same moment.** A user reading one gets "healthy", the other "corrupt". Both ship on the GA MCP surface.

## The cause no longer exists

I scanned **every** `manifest.json` under the brain data directory — **35 files, 0 contain `suppressed_warnings`**. The current `devenv` manifest is `schema_version: 3` with a `warnings` key and no such field.

So the component has been pinned to `failed` since **2026-10-11** — four days — for a condition that is no longer true, and nothing retries it or clears the state.

## What is NOT the bug

The strict/tolerant split is **deliberate and correct**, and should not be "fixed":

- `loadBrainManifest` (readers) tolerates unknown fields.
- `loadBrainManifestForReplace` (writers) refuses them, because "re-encoding from a struct that never saw them erases what another build recorded. Availability is the reader's concern; not destroying state is this one's."

`patterns` is a writer, so refusing was right. `isUnknownFieldError` also works — the prefix `json: unknown field ` matches the raw decoder error, and the tolerant path exists as far back as v0.1.0.

## The three real defects

1. **The message blames corruption for a recoverable, understood condition.** `memory_state_corrupt` reads as data loss. The truth is "another build wrote a field this build does not know, and a writer will not silently erase it." Same class as COR-2150 and COR-2146: a correct refusal reported uselessly, with no remedy named.
2. **The failure is sticky.** Once recorded, it survives the cause disappearing. Nothing re-tries, so a transient becomes permanent.
3. **Two surfaces disagree**, and neither defers to the other.

## Done when

The refusal names the unknown field and the remedy instead of saying corrupt; a component failure is re-evaluated rather than latched; and `brain_status` and `brain_patterns_status` cannot report contradictory health for the same component (a test should assert they agree).

input.title: MCP exposes 36 tools and neither of the two the agent guide tells agents to use
input.description:
Found by dogfooding the MCP surface as a coding agent, 2026-10-16.

## The repo's own guide instructs agents to do two things

From `.entire/agent-guide.md`, both marked ALWAYS:

> Retrieve prior decisions, rejected approaches and rationale with **recall** […] `entire brain recall "<question>" --json`

> When you establish something durable […] **RECORD it before finishing** […] Over MCP the same write is the **brain_remember** tool, which requires path.

## Neither exists on the MCP surface

The server exposes **36 `brain_*` tools**. `brain_remember` is **not among them**, and neither is `brain_recall`. The guide names `brain_remember` explicitly as the MCP write, so this is not a naming guess.

Both exist on the CLI and work:

```
recall      Retrieve durable facts matching a query for the current branch
remember    Record a durable fact about this repository
facts       Review, promote, and garbage-collect durable facts
```

Verified end to end via the CLI: wrote three facts, then retrieved each one by a distinct query (3/3 hits).

## Why this matters more than a missing tool

An agent driven through MCP — which is the GA integration — **cannot write a fact at all**, and cannot run the retrieval the guide mandates for prior decisions. It can only read.

That is a plausible explanation for the empty corpora. On this machine the `gh/entirehq/devenv` brain reports:

```
"facts": { "facts": 1, "distilled": 0, "authored": 1 }
"conversation": { "exchanges": 0, "vector_state": "disabled" }
```

One fact, zero distilled, after months of sessions. Brain's episodic memory is the feature, and the integration most agents run through has no door to write through.

## Also worth deciding here

`brain_status` returns roughly **8,000 tokens**, most of it install plumbing (`present_unproven`, `read_only_lstat_and_permission_mode_hint`, per-directory writability prose). An agent calling it twice spends a meaningful slice of its window on diagnostics it did not ask for. A default-terse status with the forensic detail behind a flag would make the tool usable in a normal task.

input.description:
**Corrected after reading the source. My first write-up of this was wrong in a way that matters.**

I reported that MCP exposes no way to write a fact. Half of that is wrong, and the correct version is a stronger argument for cutting a release.

## What is actually true

| | v0.1.0 (released) | main |
|---|---|---|
| `brain_*` tools declared | **36** | **37** |
| `brain_remember` | **absent** | **present** (`mcp.go:906`) |
| `brain_recall` | absent | **absent** |

`brain_remember` was added in **`03655cc0` — "feat(mcp): let an agent record a durable fact"**. It is fully implemented: declaration, dispatch case, and a deliberate design where `path` is **required** rather than agent-classified, with the reasoning in-code:

> "Required rather than inferred, and refused rather than guessed: the CLI's fallback classifies by shelling out to a coding agent, and an MCP call must not spend model tokens its caller did not ask for."

That is the right design and it is already built.

## How I confirmed which binary I was talking to

My live MCP surface listed exactly **36** `brain_*` tools with no `brain_remember` — matching v0.1.0 exactly, not main. The installed plugin reports `0.1.0`.

## Why this matters

**This is COR-2157's argument in one concrete fact.** "356 commits behind" is abstract. "The released brain cannot record a memory, and the fix has been on main for weeks" is not. Brain's episodic memory is the product; every outsider installing today gets a build whose agent integration can only read.

It also likely explains the empty corpora — this machine's `gh/entirehq/devenv` brain reports `facts: 1, distilled: 0` after months of sessions.

## What remains genuinely missing (not a release problem)

**`brain_recall` does not exist on MCP in any version.** The agent guide marks recall as ALWAYS for prior decisions and rationale, and `brain_query` is not a substitute — it searches history and docs, which is a different question. An MCP-driven agent still cannot run the retrieval the guide mandates.

Verified the CLI path works end to end: wrote 3 facts, retrieved each by a distinct query, 3/3 hits. Facts are branch-scoped, so `--branch main` matters.

## Also worth deciding

`brain_status` returns roughly **8,000 tokens**, most of it install plumbing (`present_unproven`, `read_only_lstat_and_permission_mode_hint`, per-directory writability prose). Too expensive to call casually during a task.

## Done when

1. A release ships `brain_remember` (see COR-2157).
2. `brain_recall` is added to the MCP surface.
3. A test asserts every tool the agent guide names is actually declared — this gap existed because nothing checks the guide against the surface.
4. `brain_status` has a default form small enough to call during a task.

## Root cause of the sticky failure located. It is a two-branch asymmetry in `setup_status.go`.

Both remaining defects have the same origin, and it is not a mystery any more — it is a decision.

### The five manifest-backed components self-heal

`sessions, seed, docs, semantic, history` clear a recorded failure when the source has been regenerated since the setup record was written:

```go
failure, hasFailure := failures[name]
if hasFailure && present[name] && !generated[name].Before(record.UpdatedAt) {
    hasFailure = false
}
```

### Everything else never does

`patterns, entities, memory, branches, …` are reported straight from the setup record, with no equivalent check:

```go
for _, component := range record.Components {
    ...
    state := "built"
    if component.failed() {
        state = "failed"
    }
```

So a failure recorded during one setup run is reported **forever**, regardless of what has happened since. That is exactly why `patterns` has read `failed` since 2026-10-11 while the triggering field is gone from all 35 manifests.

### And it explains the contradiction

The two surfaces disagree because they read **different things**:

- `brain_status` → the setup record's **historical** outcome (never re-evaluated)
- `brain_patterns_status` → the patterns artifacts **on disk** (`present: true, freshness: current`)

Neither is lying. They answer different questions and present both as "health".

### Why I stopped here rather than patching it

`setupComponent` is `{Name, State, Detail, Hint}` — **no timestamp**. There is nothing to compare against `record.UpdatedAt`, so the self-heal rule cannot simply be extended to the second branch. A fix needs one of:

**Option A — give `setupComponent` a timestamp.** Smallest change, symmetric with the existing rule, and the staleness logic becomes one shared helper instead of two branches. Costs a field on a persisted record, so old records have a zero value that must be treated as "unknown", not "stale".

**Option B — ask each subsystem for live state**, the way `brain_patterns_status` already does. Strictly more correct, removes the contradiction by construction rather than by convention, and is the larger change.

I lean **A**, because the asymmetry is the bug and A deletes it; B is a better end state but is a refactor rather than a fix.

Either way the test should assert the two surfaces **cannot** report contradictory health for the same component — that is the invariant, and nothing currently holds it.

Not implemented: picking between A and B changes a persisted record shape, which I am not willing to do unreviewed. Defect 1 (the misleading corruption message) is fixed in `2308540f`.

## The `brain_status` size problem, measured and located

Turning the vague "~8k tokens" note into something actionable.

### `compact` does nothing for MCP

The MCP handler already asks for it:

```go
runAgentStatus(ctx, cmd, opts, agentStatusOptions{json: true, details: details, compact: true, ...}, target)
```

But `agentStatusOptions` says, in its own comment:

> `verbose` selects the FULL text report. It changes rendering only: **the data gathered, and therefore `--json`, is identical either way.**

`compact` is a **text-rendering** flag. MCP always uses `json: true`, so the compactness it requests is silently a no-op, and every call returns the full payload.

### Where the bytes are

Measured on `entire-brain status --json` for this repo (13,773 bytes, ~3.4k tokens; the devenv brain is roughly twice that):

| subtree | bytes | share |
|---|---|---|
| **`/memory`** | 11,402 | **82.8%** |
| `/memory/install` | 4,129 | 30.0% |
| `/memory/schemas` | 2,440 | 17.7% |
| `/memory/locks` | 943 | 6.8% |
| `/retrieval` | 622 | 4.5% |

**One subtree is 83% of the response**, and it is maintenance forensics: per-directory `present_unproven` / `read_only_lstat_and_permission_mode_hint` prose, a compiled-vs-observed schema matrix, and lock inspection. None of it answers the question an agent calls `brain_status` to ask.

### Producer

`memoryReadOnlyHealth(brainDir, now)` (`memory_admin.go:2017`) builds the whole payload; `doctor` consumes the same thing via `brainDoctorReadOnlyReport`, which is where that depth genuinely belongs.

### There is already a precedent for excluding exactly this kind of thing

`brainStatusReport.Manifest` carries this comment:

> deliberately not part of the JSON contract: it duplicates the structured sections above and its session list scales with brain size

The `memory` forensic block is the same category — it duplicates `issues`/`sources` health and scales with install complexity rather than with anything the caller asked about.

### Suggested shape

Give `agentStatusOptions` a `forensics` flag that affects **data, not just rendering**, drop `install`/`schemas`/`locks` from the status payload when it is false, and have MCP pass `forensics: details`. Default MCP status drops to roughly a sixth of its current size; anyone wanting the forensics passes `details: true` or uses `doctor`, which already exists for that.

**Not implemented.** Threading a flag through the health builder changes what a GA tool returns by default, and that is a contract change worth doing deliberately rather than as a late-night side effect. The measurement above is the hard part; the change itself is small once the shape is agreed.

**1. I had #367/#368 exactly backwards.** Earlier I called them *"the only two PRs with 0 failing checks — the cheapest proof that merging works."* Wrong. They have **zero of the 18 required checks**. No failures because **nothing ran**.

They're from **`garvit-arora`, a FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR on a fork**. GitHub held the workflows at `action_required` — they've sat **2 days waiting for one click**. For a project trying to GA to outsiders, that's the worst PR to leave hanging. Both are also **126 commits behind main**.

**2. `UNSTABLE` ≠ broken.** Every "READY*" above is mergeable with only `Entire Gates` red, and **Entire Gates is not a required check**. All 18 required checks pass. The gate is noise for merge purposes.

## What "everything ready" needs

1. **Approve CI** on #367 and #368 — one click each, then they're real.
2. **Refresh 6 conflicting branches** against main: #345, #321, #374, #329, #344, #352. I did #351 this way already; conflicts were 1–3 files each, ~15 min total.
3. **#365 gets measured separately** — it changes which facts come back.
4. **Then** the release decisions: version number, the three stray local tags.

invited to paste as a space is, and $ and backtick still EXPAND inside the
double quotes a naive fix reaches for. main narrowed the trigger back to
space/tab/quote while extracting a shellSingleQuote helper.

the body: shellSingleQuote is byte-identical to the inline form used here,
so nothing is lost by sharing it, and quoting more than strictly necessary
is free -- a single-quoted token is valid wherever a bare one was.

"/tmp/a;rm -rf /", /tmp/a|b and "/tmp/a b" all come back single-quoted,
and a plain path still comes back bare. Under main's narrowed set the
first four would have been emitted unquoted.

## #329 cannot be merged mechanically — it and main made opposite product calls

I refreshed five of the six conflicting PRs against main tonight. **I deliberately left #329 alone**, because its conflict is not a merge mechanic.

### The disagreement

`verify_cmd_test.go` conflicts as two test names stating opposite positions:

| branch | test | position |
|---|---|---|
| **#329** | `TestStatusDetailsIncludesVerificationSummary` | verification belongs on `status`, gated behind `--details` |
| **main** | `TestFactVerificationBelongsToDoctorNotStatus` | verification belongs to **doctor**, not status at all |

This is not just naming. **main does not call `populateBrainStatusVerification` from `agent_surface.go` at all** — I checked. It removed the call and wrote a test asserting the placement. #329 keeps the call and gates it.

Both have a real argument, which is why I won't pick:

- **#329's case** (from its own comment): the walk is `git cat-file -e` plus `git for-each-ref --contains` over heads/remotes/tags per distinct anchor commit — refs × history, seconds to a minute on a repo with real history. It made it opt-in rather than removing it, so `brain verify` and `status --details` still pay it while the default path does not.
- **main's case**: `brain status` is what the docs point session-start hooks and the MCP `brain_status` tool at, and the safest way to guarantee the default never pays that cost is for the code not to be on that path at all.

### Why I stopped rather than choosing

Taking main's side silently deletes a feature #329 intended. Taking #329's side silently reinstates a cost main deliberately removed, against a test that exists to prevent exactly that. Either one is the failure mode this whole stack has been fixing: a merge that erases another branch's deliberate decision.

### What I need

One line from you or #329's author: **does fact verification live on `status --details`, or only on `doctor`?**

Once that is settled the merge is mechanical — the other six files in #329 are resolved shapes I already applied on sibling branches (the shell-quoting widening is identical to #321's, the `distill_cmd.go` and `git_harden.go` collisions are both "keep both sides", and `semantic.go`/`verify_cmd.go` are pure additions with an empty main side).

**#329's branch is untouched, exactly as its author pushed it.**

## #367 has never been tested, and it is one click from being unblocked

I previously described this PR as having "0 failing checks" and called it one of the safest merges. **That was exactly backwards.**

It has **zero of the 18 required checks** — no failures because **nothing ran**:

```
test | completed | action_required | 2026-10-14T11:17:10Z
```

`action_required` means the workflow was queued and never approved. The reason:

```
#367 author=garvit-arora  assoc=FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR  fork=garvit-arora/entire-brain
```

GitHub holds workflow runs for first-time contributors on forks until a maintainer approves them. It has been waiting since **2026-10-14**.

### Two consequences

1. **Nothing is known about this change.** The claim in the PR that the invocations are pinned by regression tests is untested here — those tests have never executed in CI.
2. The branch is **126 commits behind main**, so even once approved it needs a refresh before the result means anything.

### Worth saying plainly

This is an **outside contribution to a project whose P0 is "someone outside the team can install and run it"** (COR-2157). Two first-time-contributor PRs sitting two days behind an approval button is a bad look for exactly the audience this milestone is about — and it is the cheapest thing on this board to fix.

**Action: approve the workflow run on #367 and #368, then refresh both against main.** I can do the refresh; the approval needs a maintainer.

input.body:
## Correction: hiding the aliases is NOT the free, mechanical step I called it

I said step 1 needed no decision and that I could just do it. I checked before doing it, and that was wrong.

**All six aliases are referenced in documentation**, outside tests and outside `mcp.go`:

| alias | non-test files referencing it | includes |
|---|---|---|
| `brain_search` | **11** | `docs/reference.md`, `docs/memory_lifecycle_plan.md` |
| `brain_vsearch` | 7 | `docs/reference.md`, `docs/memory_lifecycle_plan.md` |
| `brain_search_code` | 3 | `docs/reference.md`, **`docs/getting-started.md`** |
| `brain_index_status` | 2 | `docs/reference.md`, `docs/semantic_mcp_guide.md` |
| `brain_detect_changes` | 1 | `docs/semantic_mcp_guide.md` |
| `brain_get_architecture` | 1 | `docs/semantic_mcp_guide.md` |

## Why this changes the plan rather than just adding work

Hiding a tool the docs still teach **creates the exact defect class of COR-2147** — "generated agent guides must use commands the released Graph actually has". That issue exists because we shipped guidance naming a command the user's build did not expose. Hiding `brain_search` while `docs/reference.md` and `getting-started.md` still teach it reproduces that, in our own docs, on the onboarding path for the outsiders M5 is about.

`brain_search_code` appearing in **`getting-started.md`** is the sharpest version: that is the first page a new user reads.

## Revised step 1

Not "hide the aliases". It is:

1. Repoint all 11+ doc references at the canonical tool (`brain_query` with `keyword: true`, `brain_code`, `brain_changes`, `brain_get_graph_schema`, `brain_status`).

because the same key meaning two amounts is a client bug."

signature being valid forever."

D=$(cat "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/acme_build.txt"); cd "$D"
cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Acme Payments

A small, deliberately realistic payments service — used as a **demo space for
Entire Brain**.

It is here so Brain has something true to index: real packages, real call
relationships, real HTTP routes, and a handful of design decisions whose
*reasons* are not visible in the code. That last part is the point. Anyone can
read `Create` and see that an idempotency key is required. Only the recorded
history says **why** a reused key with a different body is refused instead of
honoured.

## What it does

```
POST /v1/charges              create a charge (Idempotency-Key required)
GET  /v1/charges/{id}         read one charge
GET  /v1/charges/{id}/ledger  the append-only journal for that charge
POST /v1/webhooks/provider    signed provider callbacks
GET  /healthz
```

## Layout

| package | responsibility |
|---|---|
| `internal/money` | exact amounts in minor units |
| `internal/charge` | charge creation, idempotency, capture |
| `internal/ledger` | append-only double-entry journal |
| `internal/webhook` | signature verification + callback handling |
| `internal/store` | persistence seam (in-memory implementation) |
| `internal/api` | HTTP routes |

## Run it

```bash
go test ./...
go run ./cmd/payments        # ADDR=:8080 by default
```

## The decisions worth asking Brain about

Each of these is recorded as a durable fact, so `entire brain recall` can
answer the *why* rather than re-deriving it from the code:

1. **Amounts are int64 minor units, never float.** `0.10` has no exact float
   representation, so a thousand dime charges drift from the receipt.
2. **The idempotency key is required, not optional.** A lost response is
   indistinguishable from a failure, so clients retry — and an unkeyed retry
   is a second charge.
3. **A reused key with a different body is an error, not a new charge.**
4. **The ledger is append-only.** A refund is a new entry pair; nothing is
   ever edited, so the balance is replayable.
5. **Webhook secrets are a set, not a value** — rotation needs an overlap
   window or real traffic gets rejected mid-rollout.
6. **An early capture returns 409, not 200 or 500.** The provider's callback
   can beat our own write; 409 asks for a retry, 200 loses the event, 500 gets
   the endpoint disabled.

Try:

```bash
entire brain recall "why is the idempotency key required" --json
entire brain recall "why 409 and not 500 on an early capture" --json
entire graph query --repo . --query "where are charges captured"
entire graph impact --repo . --symbol Capture
```
EOF

input.command:
D=$(cat "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/acme_build.txt"); cd "$D"; mkdir -p scripts
cat > scripts/seed-brain.sh <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Seed this repo's Entire Brain with the design decisions behind the code.
#
# Durable facts live in YOUR LOCAL brain, not in git. The default fact backend
# (local-gitmeta) is explicitly "fully local, no network", so cloning this repo
# does NOT bring the facts with it. Run this once after cloning and `brain recall`
# will answer the "why" questions the README lists.
#
#   ./scripts/seed-brain.sh
#
# Facts are BRANCH-SCOPED, which is why every call passes --branch main: a fact
# recorded on a feature branch is invisible to someone sitting on main.
#
# Running this twice records the facts twice. It is a seed, not a sync.
set -euo pipefail

BRAIN="${ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN:-$HOME/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin/entire-brain}"
BRANCH="${BRANCH:-main}"

if [ ! -x "$BRAIN" ]; then
  echo "entire-brain not found at $BRAIN" >&2
  echo "install it:  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/entireio/entire-brain/main/scripts/get-brain.sh | bash" >&2
  exit 1
fi

remember() { # <path> <kind> <text>
  "$BRAIN" remember "$3" --path "$1" --kind "$2" --branch "$BRANCH" --json >/dev/null
  echo "  recorded: $1"
}

echo "Seeding durable facts on branch '$BRANCH'..."

remember architecture.money.decision decision \
'Amounts are int64 MINOR units (cents), never float64. float64 cannot represent 0.10 exactly, so summing a thousand dime charges drifts from the figure the customer was shown, and a ledger that disagrees with the receipt is not a ledger. money.Currency carries an Exponent so JPY renders with no decimals and USD with two.'

remember architecture.charge.decision decision \
'The Idempotency-Key header is REQUIRED on charge creation, not optional. A payments API runs over a network that loses responses, so a client cannot distinguish a timeout from a success and will retry; an unkeyed retry is a second charge against one intent. Refusing the request with 400 is better than taking the money and arguing later.'

remember architecture.charge.invariant invariant \
'A replay with the same Idempotency-Key but a DIFFERENT body returns ErrKeyReusedWithNewBody (HTTP 409), not a new charge. One key meaning two amounts is a client bug, and quietly honouring the second would charge an amount the first caller never agreed to.'

remember architecture.ledger.invariant invariant \
'The ledger is append-only double-entry: entries are never updated or deleted, and a refund is a NEW entry pair rather than an edit to the original. That keeps the balance derivable by replay, which is what makes a dispute answerable months later. Both sides are appended in a single Append call so a crash cannot leave the journal unbalanced.'

remember architecture.webhook.decision decision \
'Webhook verification holds a SET of secrets, not one value, because rotation needs an overlap window: during a rollout the provider may still sign with the previous secret, and a verifier holding only the newest rejects real traffic for the length of the rotation.'

remember constraints.webhook.invariant invariant \
'Webhook signature comparison uses hmac.Equal, never ==. A byte-by-byte string compare returns as soon as it finds a mismatch, so its timing reveals how much of the prefix was correct and a few thousand attempts recover the signature.'

remember architecture.webhook.gotcha gotcha \
'GOTCHA: the provider can deliver charge.captured BEFORE our own Create has committed - their network hop is often faster than our write. The handler answers store.ErrNotFound with HTTP 409, not 500 and not 200. 409 makes the provider retry with backoff and the charge exists by the next delivery; 200 makes it stop retrying and the capture is lost; 500 gets the endpoint marked unhealthy and disabled.'

remember architecture.charge.invariant invariant \
'Capture is idempotent on purpose: a second charge.captured for an already-captured charge returns nil without writing ledger entries again. Providers retry webhooks as normal traffic, so treating a duplicate as an error or re-appending the pair would double the recorded revenue.'

echo
echo "Done. Try:"
echo "  entire brain recall \"why is the idempotency key required\" --json"
echo "  entire brain recall \"why 409 and not 500 on an early capture\" --json"
SCRIPT
