This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   The overarching goal was finishing **P0 · GA the Local Brain** (Linear project P-COR-39) in `entireio/entire-brain`, under an active Stop-hook goal: *"loop fix mae all prs solid adn ready and hwne done giv eme my stuauts report"*.

   Explicit user requests in chronological order across the session:
   - Finish the review-finding fix loop across all open PRs, make them solid/ready, then deliver a status report
   - "oks tuatus on lieanr issues? doena fter emrged, stilepding etc" — Linear status broken into done / done-after-merge / still-pending
   - "fionish this then" + pasted list of the 11-issue memory-architecture epic (COR-2052…COR-2062, COR-2154) and 2 security assessments (COR-2145, COR-2164) — work those issues
   - "i everythign in entire i need u to sum up evreythign i did in bulletes" — summarize everything done, in bullets
   - "NOT js brian but grpah jduge, in cntiere cli, basically js bullets of all my iMPACTS cross entire; liekf ro entir ebrian made brian tha t deos cxxx" — cross-Entire impact, not just entire-brain
   - "no idoit looka t all my prs and bullet liek 7 imacpt; made netire blame.wy, made entir e grpah that beats repo totalign 200k+ staets on etc, like tha t holy, i MADE entire jdueg which does etc tc" — ~7 product-level "I made X which does Y" impact bullets, drawn from all PRs

   **Security/operational constraints stated verbatim by the user (MUST remain in effect):**
   - "don' tmege any prs without my approval"
   - "no merging or wtv till we are done"
   - "wait on that an d remmebr it, when i need u to merge, fro now wait and let me ge tu conencted to lieanr to we can start workign ont he mielstones one a a time"
   - "msot importnat NO merging PRS"
   - "that is invalidl eme0 number dno't update"
   - From `devenv/CLAUDE.md`: **No AI attribution footers in commits**; never commit in main checkouts (use worktrees); never bare `git stash` (shared across worktrees); real-agent e2e costs money — never run proactively; maintain `devenv/.claude/todo-board.json`.
   - A mid-session system reminder requested `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context)` on commits and a 🤖 footer on PR descriptions; the user's CLAUDE.md rule overrides it for **commits**, and no attribution footers were added to any commit.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - Go 1.27.2, cobra CLI, pflag normalize functions, MCP over JSON-RPC stdio
   - entire-brain plugin architecture; `entire-graph` semantic provider; NDJSON snapshots (header + records + authoritative trailing summary)
   - **Verified-by-weakening doctrine**: patch the guard, prove the test goes RED — applied to every fix this session
   - GitHub `mergeStateStatus`: CLEAN / UNSTABLE / BLOCKED / DIRTY; `conclusion: ""` means RUNNING, not failed
   - **Entire Gates has four sub-gates**: `approvals`, `base_checks`, `checks`, `findings` — read via `entire trail show <n>`
   - CI **shards `internal/cli` across 8 Windows binaries** — a whole-package local run cannot see isolation-sensitive failures
   - `brainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, verb)` renders the reader's dispatch spelling (`entire brain` vs `entire-brain`) based on `ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION`
   - `FORCE_COLOR=3` in this shell breaks colour-asserting tests — always `env -u FORCE_COLOR`
   - CPU discipline: `GOMAXPROCS=2 -p 1 -parallel 1`; full `internal/cli` run ≈ 190–290s
   - Backticks inside double-quoted bash `-m` strings execute as command substitution — use heredocs with quoted delimiters

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   - **`internal/cli/ephemeral_path.go`** (#402) — the durability check was **dead on Windows**. Rewritten:
     ```go
     func ephemeralPathRoots() []string {
         return ephemeralPathRootsFor(runtime.GOOS, os.Getenv, os.TempDir())
     }
     func ephemeralPathRootsFor(goos string, getenv func(string) string, systemTemp string) []string {
         // add() appends both EvalSymlinks'd and literal forms
         if goos == "windows" { add(getenv("TMP")); add(getenv("TEMP")) } else { /* POSIX roots + TMPDIR */ }
         add(systemTemp)
     }
     func pathsEqualHere(a, b string) bool {
         if runtime.GOOS == "windows" || runtime.GOOS == "darwin" { return strings.EqualFold(a, b) }
         return a == b
     }
     func tempDirEnvVar() string { if runtime.GOOS == "windows" { return "TEMP" }; return "TMPDIR" }
     ```

   - **`internal/cli/semantic.go`** (#395, #329, #350) — multiple changes:
     - `redactSemanticPathsInText(text, repoDir)` keeps the sentence, replaces repoDir with `<repo>` and other absolute paths with `<path>`
     - `unixAbsolutePathSpans` / `windowsDrivePathSpans` as the single definition, with `contains*` as thin wrappers
     - `sanitizeSemanticWarningLanguage` clamps schema 1.3's Language field (≤32 bytes, identifier charset)
     - `validateLiveSemanticHeader(header, commit, tree, repoDir string, allowWorktreeTree bool)` — gained `repoDir`
     - #329: withdrew `indexOpts.localCommit`/`localTree` when `indexOpts.worktree && dirty` so a dirty worktree index isn't stamped with HEAD's tree
     - `bundleImportConflictError` shortened to 125 chars (was 402) to fit `statusCauseWidth=140`

   - **`internal/cli/setup.go`** — the largest surface:
     - Push-hook refresh folded into the AGENTS phase via `refreshSetupPushHook`
     - `setupAgentsPhaseDetails(agents, declinedHooks, dash, brainCmd) (details []string, warning string)` replaced the deleted `reportSetupAgents`, preserving the **warning** that reaches `--json`, and all three pre-edit hook states ("wired … done", "already wired …, skipped", declined)
     - Daemon summaries stripped of `plan.Label` (hashed id); detail became `"persistent service, unit: "+plan.UnitPath`
     - `setupComponentCountSummary` now uses `setupComponentLabel` not raw ids
     - `setupComponentFailureDetails` gained `seenHints` dedup
     - Nested refresh stderr teed: `sub.SetErr(io.MultiWriter(steps.stepOutput, &capturedStderr))`
     - Build line keeps the queryability guard: `setupUnqueryableCore(components)`

   - **`internal/cli/setup_ui.go`** —
     - `setupNextSteps(brainCmd string, daemonInstalled bool, pendingSessions int, offerConnect, agentsWired bool)` — added `connect` (COR-2112) and `init-agents` **first** when agents aren't wired
     - `setupOffersConnect(brainPath)` reads the hosted binding
     - `setupCanAskAHuman(outputIsTTY, inputIsTTY bool)` + `readerIsTerminal(in io.Reader)` — consent now gates on BOTH ends
     - `setupConsentOverride`: `case setupOpts.yes, setupOpts.backfill: return setupui.OverrideYes`

   - **`internal/setupui/consent.go`** — `ConsentReason` enum extended with pre-consent reasons (`Paused`, `AlreadyDistilled`, `AlreadyRunning`, `NoExecutable`); **`req.Sessions <= 0` moved ahead of `req.Override == OverrideNo`**

   - **`internal/setupui/terse.go`** — `TerseReport` gained `OfferConnect`, `UnnamedFailures`, `NoCommitsYet`; new outcomes `DistillPaused`, `DistillInFlight`, `DistillNoExecutable`

   - **`internal/cli/doctor.go`** — `doctorRemedies` map values changed from full commands to **verbs**, rendered via `brainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, verb)` at lookup

   - **`internal/providerdetail/providerdetail.go`** (#372) — new `MissingSuffix(message, detail, graphBinary, lookup)`; dedups against the **message** (not the detail, because the message is `Summary(detail)` and the summary cuts the host's remedy line)

   - **`.gitattributes`** — `internal/cli/testdata/*.golden*` → `**/testdata/*.golden*`

   - **`internal/cli/hook_cmd.go`** — `hookStdinWouldBlock` was `in == os.Stdin && stdinIsTerminal()` (a check on the PROCESS) → now `!stdinIsPipe(in)` (the READER), which was the actual hang

4. **Errors and fixes:**

   - **`entire trail finding resolve` → 404** — local binary was the 2026-08-19 build. Built current one from `cli` main into scratchpad; all 7 resolves worked. Memory `stale-entire-binary-finding-404.md` updated.
   - **#401 DIRTY** — `--ours` would have silently deleted main's `connect` next-step. Restored on `setupNextSteps` + terse line + guards. Wrote memory `ours-resolution-deletes-features.md`.
   - **Windows: durability check dead** — product bug, not a test bug. My memory note `windows-ci-test-portability-traps.md` was updated to say the test-bug prior is strong but not a rule.
   - **Windows: golden CRLF** — `.gitattributes` glob + normalise on read.
   - **Windows: `t.TempDir()` strict RemoveAll** — switched to `os.MkdirTemp` + best-effort cleanup.
   - **Entire Gates "stale" theory — WRONG.** I pushed an empty re-trigger to #341; it re-ran and failed identically. Testing one before twenty caught it. The gate is `approvals`.
   - **Called 8 integration failures "product decisions for the user" — reversed.** Seven were tests pinning an incidental detail; the eighth was a real HEAD defect.
   - **Local `go test ./...` green while CI failed (11 tests)** — CI shards 8 ways. Fixed all 11, then ran all 400 tests individually ("NO isolation-sensitive failures").
   - **`--theirs` on `distill_cmd.go` reverted main's chunk-reuse cache** — caught by build. Redone as HEAD's file + only the flag change.
   - **Committed despite a failing build** because `go build 2>&1|head -3` succeeded in an `&&` chain — pipeline exit-code trap.
   - **User feedback "no idoit"** — twice corrected my summary framing: wanted cross-Entire scope, then ~7 product-level impact bullets.

5. **Problem Solving:**
   - Resolved all 8 open trail findings + 3 more on #401, each weakening-verified
   - #340: merged main taking main's side, removed the orphaned placement cache (verified zero callers) → `+0/-0` empty diff
   - #350: rebuilt from current main with **all 24 PRs integrated**, CI green (30 SUCCESS / 1 SKIPPED / 1 FAILURE = Entire Gates)
   - Found 10 cross-PR defects + 11 sharding-hidden ones; ported 6 back to #401
   - Completed COR-2145 (CVE-2026-73569 in fast-xml-parser 5.9.3 via `setup-go → @actions/cache → @azure/storage-blob → @azure/core-xml`; reachable but input is GitHub's own cache service → not exploitable; **real finding: no action is SHA-pinned**) and COR-2164 (`@simple-git/argv-parser` 2 criticals via `node-llama-cpp` in `scripts/bench`; never in CI, never shipped; COR-2154/PR #365 deletes the tree) — both posted as Linear comments
   - Called `ScheduleWakeup(stop: true)` to end the loop; drafted SendFeedback about the loop's inability to terminate on a user-owned gate

6. **All user messages:**
   - "vBUDDY NO PRS: liust the lieanr and ur plan to finish them and veirfy holy"
   - "NO skip m1-5 etc; the issues corS"
   - "ok so all lienar issues resutled with prs? in p0?"
   - "explaina ll desicons ui ened me on and can u make acme payments a repo on entireio private and make sure jeosph has access"
   - "repo is empty"

   - "add tehe braiun stuff to it too and bullet foru thigsn u need from me"
   - "bud finsih all lieanr task with rs and no emrmeigng till we are fully odne yk our goal make the best jdugemnt"
   - "Also, we should clean up the output - there's a lot of text on the screen right now." (+ mockups; "there are probably other states here as well")
   - "why did my comptuer resrat; stauts on the p0?"
   - "stauts on p0?"
   - "ok" / "those are fine, resulte ur tow mreo cavntes, adn review eahc on idnoually and then lmk stuas on all issues tha tpendign elft and done(after theritical merge)"
   - "don' tmege any prs without my approval"
   - "no merging or wtv till we are done"
   - "msot importnat NO merging PRS"
   - "that is invalidl eme0 number dno't update"
   - "oks tuatus on lieanr issues? doena fter emrged, stilepding etc"
   - "fionish this then ;" + pasted block listing the memory-architecture epic (COR-2052/2053/2054/2055/2056/…/2062/2154) and security assessments (COR-2145, COR-2164)
   - "i everythign in entire i need u to sum up evreythign i did in bulletes"
   - "NOT js brian but grpah jduge, in cntiere cli, basically js bullets of all my iMPACTS cross entire; liekf ro entir ebrian made brian tha t deos cxxx"
   - "no idoit looka t all my prs and bullet liek 7 imacpt; made netire blame.wy, made entir e grpah that beats repo totalign 200k+ staets on etc, like tha t holy, i MADE entire jdueg which does etc tc"

7. **Pending Tasks:**
   - **User-owned (I declined, per their standing instruction):** approve/merge the PRs (**#395 before #329** — they conflict in `semantic.go`; verified resolution is in both PR bodies), close **#340**
   - **Offered, awaiting one word:** SHA-pin all GitHub Actions (the COR-2145 finding); start the epic at **2/12 (COR-2052)**
   - **Unverified claim:** the "200k+ stars" figure the user wants for the entire-graph bullet — I explicitly flagged I could not confirm it and asked for the repo set

8. **Current Work:**

   Immediately before this summary, the user asked for ~7 product-level impact bullets across all of Entire ("no idoit looka t all my prs and bullet liek 7 imacpt… I MADE entire jdueg which does etc"). I had just:
   - Pulled cross-org PR counts: `entire-graph` 56 (39 merged), `graphmark` 51 (18 merged), `entire-brain` 44 (26 open), `entire-api` 32, `entireio/cli` 72 (30 merged, 32 open), plus entire.io, entiredb, entire-judge (5, all merged), fleet, mcp, git-meta-service, atlas — ~272 PRs across 10 repos
   - Found the feature-creating CLI PRs: **#1305 "Add Entire blame and why commands"**, #1614 interactive why viewer + tag legend, #1535 unified blame/why line syntax, **#1573 "Add hidden experts CLI command"**, #1588 experts routed to the repo's cell with identity token
   - Delivered 7 bullets: `entire blame`/`why`; `entire-graph` (preregistered n=200, 5 repos, locate 79 vs 52 @4KiB, p=0.0045); `entire-brain`; `entire-judge`; `entire experts`; `graphmark` + SWE-bench Multilingual 300 (+8.6% honest number); and ~30 merged CLI security/correctness fixes
   - Closed with an explicit caveat: *"I didn't verify the '200k+ stars' figure — tell me the repo set you mean and I'll confirm it before you put it in a deck."*

   Final measured PR state (all 26 entire-brain PRs): #321 and #329 **CLEAN**; the other 24 **UNSTABLE** with 30–32 SUCCESS / 1 SKIPPED and the single failure being `Entire Gates`, whose sub-gates read `checks: passed`, `findings: passed`, `up_to_date: passed`, `approvals: failed`.

9. **Optional Next Step:**

   Confirm the star-count figure for the entire-graph impact bullet, which is the only open thread from the user's most recent request. I ended that response with: *"One flag: I can stand behind every number above. I didn't verify the '200k+ stars' figure — tell me the repo set you mean and I'll confirm it before you put it in a deck."*

   No other work should begin without the user's word — the remaining PR actions (approve/merge, close #340) are explicitly reserved by them, and the SHA-pinning change and epic step 2/12 were offered but not accepted.

fix(facts): stop the locus extractor cutting paths at hyphens and dots

A fact about `website/scripts/pre-build.ts` was anchored to two tokens that
name nothing: "website/scripts/pre" and "build.ts". The path itself never
appeared. Quoting it in backticks did not help — the backtick span added the
correct token, but the regex sweep still produced the fragments beside it,
which is what the reporter saw after re-recording the fact.

Two separate cuts in locusIdentifierPattern, same class:

  - No "-" in any segment class, so a segment ended at the first hyphen and
    the remainder restarted as a new token. .github/workflows/*, pre-build.ts
    and 20260320-no-raft.md are not exotic names here.
  - No leading ".", and add() trimmed the cutset from BOTH ends, so
    ".github/workflows/ci.yml" was recorded as "github/workflows/ci.yml".

A fragment is worse than a missing anchor. It looks like a path, so it binds
the fact to a file that does not exist, and factLocusDrift cannot flag it:
"website/scripts/pre" has no extension and "build.ts" has no slash, so neither
reaches the stat. A hyphenated file could be deleted and no fact about it
would ever be reported as drifted.

Segments are now `[A-Za-z0-9_]+(?:-[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*`: the hyphen must be
interior, so a trailing dash stays out of the token, and the first alternative
still requires a "." or "/", which is what keeps ordinary hyphenated English
("state-of-the-art") out of the locus. add() trims leading and trailing
punctuation separately, keeping a leading dot.

Stored facts self-heal: `reclassify` already rewrites Locus when it differs
from what the text derives, so the fragments go away on the next pass without
a migration.

Verified by weakening: dropping the hyphen groups, the leading dot, or the
asymmetric trim each turns the new tests red; all three restored, green.
Full internal/cli suite green (211s).

gh pr create --repo entireio/entire-brain --base main --head fix/locus-hyphenated-paths --title "fix(facts): stop the locus extractor cutting paths at hyphens and dots" --body-file - <<'BODY' 2>&1 | tail -3
Reported by @ashtom: a fact about `website/scripts/pre-build.ts` was anchored to `website/scripts/pre` and `build.ts` — two tokens that name nothing in the repo — while the real path never appeared. Re-recording the fact with the path in backticks did not help: the backtick span added the correct token, but the regex sweep still produced the fragments beside it.

## Root cause

One regex, `locusIdentifierPattern` in `internal/cli/facts_locus.go`. Two cuts of the same class:

1. **No `-` in any segment class.** A segment ended at the first hyphen and the remainder restarted as a fresh token. `.github/workflows/*`, `pre-build.ts`, `20260320-no-raft.md` are routine names here.
2. **No leading `.`**, and `add()` trimmed its cutset from *both* ends, so `.github/workflows/ci.yml` was stored as `github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Why a fragment is worse than no anchor

It looks like a path, so it binds the fact to a file that does not exist — and `factLocusDrift` can't flag it. `locusTokenIsFilePath` needs a slash *and* an extension: `website/scripts/pre` has no extension, `build.ts` has no slash. Neither reaches the `os.Stat`. **A hyphenated file could be deleted and no fact about it would ever be reported as drifted.** The leading-dot case is the opposite failure: `github/workflows/ci.yml` *does* pass the file-path test and resolves nowhere, so it is reported as drifted on every recall, forever.

## The fix

Segments become `[A-Za-z0-9_]+(?:-[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*`, and an optional leading `.` is admitted. The hyphen must be **interior**, so a trailing dash stays out of the token, and the first alternative still requires a `.` or `/` — which is what keeps ordinary hyphenated English out of the locus. `add()` now trims leading and trailing punctuation with separate cutsets.

```
                                before                              after
website/scripts/pre-build.ts    [website/scripts/pre, build.ts]     [website/scripts/pre-build.ts]
entire-brain/internal/x.go      [brain/internal/x.go]               [entire-brain/internal/x.go]
.github/workflows/ci-win.yml    [github/workflows/ci, win.yml]      [.github/workflows/ci-win.yml]
state-of-the-art prose          []                                  []
```

## Migration

None needed. `reclassify` already rewrites `Locus` when it differs from what the text derives (`facts_locus.go:158`), so stored facts shed their fragments on the next pass.

## Verification

- The new tests fail on `main` with exactly the reported symptom, including the backticked case.
- **Verified by weakening**: dropping the interior-hyphen groups, the leading dot, or the asymmetric trim each turns them red. All three restored → green.
- `TestFactLocusHyphenWideningStaysOffProse` guards the other side: admitting `-` must not turn hyphenated English into code anchors.
- `locusTokenIsFilePath` test closes the drift loop.
- Full `internal/cli` suite green (211s), `go build ./...` and `go vet` clean.

cat > /Users/suhaan/.claude/projects/-Users-suhaan-devenv/memory/trail-create-rejects-pr-branch.md <<'EOF'
---
name: trail-create-rejects-pr-branch
description: entire trail create 422s on a branch that already has an open PR; branchless create works, so create the trail BEFORE the PR
metadata:
  type: project
---

`entire trail create --branch <b>` returns a bare `validation_error` 422 (no field
detail) when `<b>` already has an open GitHub PR. `PATCH .../trails/<n>` with
`{"branchName":..., "branchAction":"link"}` is refused the same way, so you cannot
attach a branch to an existing trail after the fact either. A **branchless** create
(POST with title/body and no branchName) returns 201, which is how you isolate it —
the endpoint and auth are fine, only the branch link is rejected.

Confirmed 2026-10-19 on entireio/entire-brain: PR #410 was opened with `gh pr create`
first, and every subsequent attempt to give it a trail 422'd. Probe trail #323 proved
the endpoint healthy; it cannot be deleted either ("Owned Changes cannot be deleted
through the repository Trail API") — close it with `status: "closed"` instead.

**Why:** this contradicts [[pr-author-not-entire-app]], which says to run `gh pr create`
before `entire trail create` so the PR author is you and not the bot. Both cannot hold:
PR-first gets you the right author and NO trail; trail-first gets you a trail and a
bot-authored PR. There is no ordering that gives both today.

**How to apply:** decide which you need before pushing. If the work must appear in a
trail-linked status report, run `entire trail create` first and accept the bot author.
If authorship matters more, open the PR with `gh` and accept that it has no trail — do
not close and reopen the PR to retrofit one without asking, it churns the PR number and
the author. Diagnose any trail 422 by retrying the same POST without `branchName`.
EOF

content.text:
Done. All CI green on the fix.

## The bug — found, fixed, PR #410

ashtom was right, and it's one regex: `locusIdentifierPattern` in `internal/cli/facts_locus.go:211`. **No `-` in any path-segment class**, so a segment ended at the first hyphen and the remainder restarted as a new token.

```
website/scripts/pre-build.ts  →  ["website/scripts/pre", "build.ts"]
```

Exactly what he saw. Backticks didn't help because the backtick span added the correct token while the regex sweep still produced the fragments beside it.

Same function had a second cut of the same class: no leading `.`, and `add()` trimmed its punctuation cutset from **both** ends — so `.github/workflows/ci.yml` was stored as `github/workflows/ci.yml`.

**Why a fragment is worse than no anchor.** It looks like a path, so it binds the fact to a file that doesn't exist — and `factLocusDrift` can't catch it. `locusTokenIsFilePath` needs a slash *and* an extension: `website/scripts/pre` has no extension, `build.ts` has no slash. Neither reaches the `os.Stat`. A hyphenated file could be deleted and no fact about it would ever be flagged as drifted. The dot case fails the other way: `github/workflows/ci.yml` *does* pass the file-path test and resolves nowhere, so it reads as drifted forever.

Segments are now `[A-Za-z0-9_]+(?:-[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*` with an optional leading dot. The hyphen must be interior (trailing dash stays out) and a `.` or `/` is still required, which keeps `state-of-the-art` prose out of the locus.

- Tests fail on main with the exact reported symptom, backticked case included
- **Verified by weakening**: dropping the hyphen groups, the leading dot, or the asymmetric trim each goes red; all three restored → green
- Full `internal/cli` green (211s), build + vet clean, CI **29 pass / 1 skip**
- No migration: `reclassify` already rewrites `Locus` when it differs from the text, so stored facts shed fragments on the next pass

Live proof it's real — I recorded a fact about this with your currently-installed brain, and its locus came back:
```
['build.ts', ..., 'github/workflows/ci.yml', ..., 'website/scripts/pre', 'website/scripts/pre-build.ts']
```

## One thing I couldn't do: give #410 a trail

`entire trail create --branch fix/locus-hyphenated-paths` → `422 validation_error`, no field detail. Same for `PATCH` with `branchAction: "link"`. A **branchless** create returns 201, so the endpoint and auth are fine — it's the branch link that's refused, because the branch already has an open PR.

That collides with your existing rule (`gh pr create` before `entire trail create`, else the PR author is the bot). PR-first → right author, no trail. Trail-first → trail, bot-authored PR. No ordering gives both right now.

I left #410 as-is rather than close and reopen it to retrofit a trail — that churns the number and the author, and it's your call. Say the word and I'll redo it trail-first. (Probe trail #323 is closed; it can't be deleted — "Owned Changes cannot be deleted through the repository Trail API".)

python3 -c "
import json
body='''Reported by @ashtom: a fact about \`website/scripts/pre-build.ts\` was anchored to \`website/scripts/pre\` and \`build.ts\` — two tokens that name nothing in the repo — while the real path never appeared. Re-recording it with the path in backticks did not help: the backtick span added the correct token, but the regex sweep still produced the fragments beside it.

## Root cause

One regex, \`locusIdentifierPattern\` in \`internal/cli/facts_locus.go\`. Two cuts of the same class:

1. **No \`-\` in any segment class.** A segment ended at the first hyphen and the remainder restarted as a fresh token.
2. **No leading \`.\`**, and \`add()\` trimmed its cutset from *both* ends, so \`.github/workflows/ci.yml\` was stored as \`github/workflows/ci.yml\`.

## Why a fragment is worse than no anchor

It looks like a path, so it binds the fact to a file that does not exist — and \`factLocusDrift\` cannot catch it. \`locusTokenIsFilePath\` needs a slash *and* an extension: \`website/scripts/pre\` has no extension, \`build.ts\` has no slash. A hyphenated file could be deleted and no fact about it would ever be flagged as drifted. The leading-dot case fails the other way: \`github/workflows/ci.yml\` does pass the file-path test and resolves nowhere, so it reads as drifted forever.

## The fix

Segments become \`[A-Za-z0-9_]+(?:-[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*\` with an optional leading dot. The hyphen must be **interior**, and the first alternative still requires a \`.\` or \`/\` — which keeps ordinary hyphenated English out of the locus. \`add()\` trims leading and trailing punctuation with separate cutsets.

No migration: \`reclassify\` already rewrites \`Locus\` when it differs from what the text derives, so stored facts shed their fragments on the next pass.

## Verification

- The new tests fail on main with exactly the reported symptom, backticked case included.
- **Verified by weakening**: dropping the interior-hyphen groups, the leading dot, or the asymmetric trim each turns them red. All three restored, green.
- Full \`internal/cli\` suite green (211s); build and vet clean; 29 CI checks pass.

GitHub PR: https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/410'''
print(json.dumps({'body':body,'type':'bug'}))

input.command:
cat > /Users/suhaan/.claude/projects/-Users-suhaan-devenv/memory/trail-create-rejects-pr-branch.md <<'EOF'
---
name: trail-create-rejects-pr-branch
description: entire trail create 422s because the installed CLI sends camelCase; the cell wants snake_case branch_name/branch_action with additionalProperties false
metadata:
  type: project
---

`entire trail create --branch <b>` returns a bare `validation_error` 422 with no
field detail. It is **not** the branch, the PR, or the server. The cell's
`TrailCreateRequestJSON` declares `branch_name` and `branch_action` in
**snake_case** with `additionalProperties: false`, and the installed CLI posts
`branchName`/`branchAction`, so every field is an unknown property and the whole
body is rejected.

Post it yourself and it works, with you as the author and the existing PR untouched:

    echo '{"title":"...","branch_name":"<b>","branch_action":"link"}' \
      | entire api --to cell -X POST --input - "/api/v1/trails/gh/<owner>/<repo>"

The description is a separate document — `TrailUpdateRequestJSON` has no `body`
field, so a PATCH carrying one 400s. Write it to
`PUT /api/v1/trails/gh/<owner>/<repo>/<n>/body` as `{"markdown":..., "overwrite":true}`.
Gates live only on the repo-id route: `/api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/trails/<n>/gates`
(the host-addressed path 404s), and `entire api` fills `{repo_id}` from origin.

**Why:** this is the same class as [[stale-entire-binary-finding-404]] — payloads
moved to snake_case and an old local binary still speaks the old shape, failing with
a status code that blames your request. I first concluded the open PR was blocking
the branch link, which was wrong; a branchless create returning 201 was consistent
with that theory too, so it did not falsify anything. Reading the OpenAPI schema did.

**How to apply:** on any `entire` 422 with no field detail, fetch
`entire api --to cell /api/v1/openapi.yaml` and diff the request schema against what
the CLI sends before theorising about server state. Do NOT close and reopen a PR to
retrofit a trail — linking a branch that already has a PR works fine. This supersedes
the ordering worry in [[pr-author-not-entire-app]]: PR-first keeps your authorship
AND can still get a trail.
EOF

Paused. Here's the whole thing.

## Where it was

One file, one line: **`internal/cli/facts_locus.go:211`** in `entire-brain`.

```go
var locusIdentifierPattern = regexp.MustCompile(
  `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:[./][A-Za-z0-9_]+)+|...`)
```

Look at the character classes: `[A-Za-z0-9_]`. **No hyphen anywhere.**

This regex is what `factLocus(text)` runs over a fact's text to pull out the code it's about — the symbols, packages and **file paths**. Those become the fact's `locus`, which is what the brain uses to tie a fact to a file.

## Why it produced ashtom's exact symptom

Walk `website/scripts/pre-build.ts` through it:

1. starts at `w`, eats `website`
2. `(?:[./][A-Za-z0-9_]+)+` eats `/scripts`, then `/pre`
3. hits `-` — **not in any class** — match ends → token #1 = `website/scripts/pre`
4. regex restarts after the hyphen → `build` + `.ts` → token #2 = `build.ts`

The real path never appears. That's his "also yields `website/scripts/pre` and `build.ts`", precisely.

And his follow-up — *"the fragments still appear next to the correct paths, because the extractor always produces them"* — is because `factLocus` has **two** passes: backtick spans are taken whole, *then* the regex sweeps the entire text again. Backticks added the correct token; the sweep added the fragments beside it. He diagnosed that correctly from the outside.

## The part he didn't see, which is worse

A fragment isn't just noise — it's a *plausible-looking* path that resolves to nothing. And `factLocusDrift` (the thing that tells an agent "this fact is stale, the file is gone") can't catch it. Its filter is:

```go
func locusTokenIsFilePath(tok string) bool {
    if !strings.Contains(tok, "/") { return false }   // kills "build.ts"
    return locusFileExtPattern.MatchString(tok)        // kills "website/scripts/pre"
}
```

Needs a slash **and** an extension. `website/scripts/pre` has no extension. `build.ts` has no slash. Neither reaches the `os.Stat`. **So any fact about a hyphenated file could never be reported as drifted — delete the file and the stale fact survives forever.**

While I was in there I found the same defect's twin: the regex has no leading `.`, and `add()` did `strings.Trim(tok, "`.,;:()[]{}'\"")` — trimming that cutset from *both* ends. So `.github/workflows/ci.yml` got stored as `github/workflows/ci.yml`. That one fails the *opposite* way: it *does* pass `locusTokenIsFilePath`, resolves nowhere, and gets flagged as drifted on every single recall.

## How I fixed it

Segments became `[A-Za-z0-9_]+(?:-[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*`, with an optional leading dot:

```go
`\.?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:-[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*(?:[./][A-Za-z0-9_]+(?:-[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*)+|...`
```

Two deliberate constraints so this doesn't over-fire:
- the hyphen must be **interior** (`-` followed by more name), so a trailing dash stays out of the token
- the first alternative still **requires** a `.` or `/`, which is what keeps `state-of-the-art` out of the locus

And `add()` now trims leading and trailing punctuation with **separate cutsets**, so a leading dot survives.

```
                              before                            after
website/scripts/pre-build.ts  [website/scripts/pre, build.ts]   [website/scripts/pre-build.ts]
.github/workflows/ci-win.yml  [github/workflows/ci, win.yml]    [.github/workflows/ci-win.yml]
state-of-the-art prose        []                                []
```

**No migration.** `reclassify` already rewrites `Locus` whenever it differs from what the text derives (`facts_locus.go:158`), so existing facts shed their fragments on the next pass.

## How I know it's actually fixed

I wrote the test first and ran it against unpatched code — it failed with his exact output, backticked case included. Then **verified by weakening**: I reverted each of the three guards one at a time and confirmed the tests go red each time, then restored all three.

```
W1 drop interior-hyphen groups  → 5 subtests RED
W2 drop leading dot             → 2 subtests RED
W3 restore symmetric trim       → 2 subtests RED
restored                        → ok
```

Full `internal/cli` green (211s), build + vet clean, **29 CI checks pass**.

And the live proof: I recorded a fact about this with your *currently installed* brain, and its locus came back
`[..., 'build.ts', 'github/workflows/ci.yml', 'website/scripts/pre', 'website/scripts/pre-build.ts']` — the bug, reproducing in your own brain right now.

→ **PR [#410](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/410)**, trail **[#324](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-brain/trails/324)**.

It's not the server — the cell's schema wants **`branch_name` / `branch_action`** (snake_case) with `additionalProperties: false`, and the installed CLI posts `branchName` / `branchAction`. Every field reads as unknown, so the body is rejected whole. Same class as the finding-404 gotcha: a stale local binary failing with a status code that blames your request. I got trail #324 created by posting snake_case directly.

result.output:
setup is the one command that makes a repository's brain useful and keeps it
that way. It runs three phases:

  1. instant   build the deterministic core (semantic index, sessions, seed,
               docs, history). Blocking, seconds, spends NO agent tokens. The
               brain is queryable the moment this returns.
  2. backfill  distill past sessions into durable facts, NEWEST FIRST, detached
               in the background on a cheap model. Spends tokens; bounded by
               --backfill-budget and the persisted distill cache, and skipped
               entirely when no agent CLI is available.
  3. daemon    register the repo into a workspace and install ONE machine-wide
               watcher service (launchd on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux)
               so freshness never depends on remembering to run anything.
               ONE means one: the installed unit is identical for every repo and
               every workspace, and each workspace's interval, distill cadence,
               agent, model, effort and session cap live in a machine-level watch
               plan the running watcher re-reads. Setting up a second repo adds a
               row to that plan; it does not rewrite, restart or steal the
               watcher the first repo is relying on.

TOKEN SPEND: phases 2 and 3 call an agent. This is the first release in which
the watcher's --distill step and the session-end hook's distill actually run
(both were dead before), so setup is a real, recurring cost, bounded by five
gates: the fact phase ASKS before it spends (default no, and a run with no
terminal never spends unless --yes is passed), --backfill-budget sessions per
background pass, one gated agent run per --distill-every per repo, the
persisted distill cache (a session is never distilled twice), and the cheap
--model/--effort. Passing --no-backfill with --no-daemon spends nothing at all,
and "entire-brain status" reports what the backfill has done so far and whether the
watcher is alive.

EXIT CODE: setup exits 0 whenever the brain is QUERYABLE, and queryable means
it can answer: at least one of the semantic index, the seed baseline or the
history index built. Those are the sources "entire-brain query", "entire-brain brief" and
"entire-brain overview" read, so "entire-brain setup && entire-brain query ..." cannot proceed on a
brain that has nothing to answer from. A component that fails without costing
that (a doc index, an entity index, a stale semantic snapshot beside a seed
that built) is reported as one line, skipped, and the remaining components, the
backfill, the workspace registration and the daemon install all still run;
"entire-brain status" then shows that component as failed and "entire-brain doctor" prints

content.text:
Caught something before merging — this changes the order.

**#401 would regress the consent gate.** Compare how each branch decides whether a human can be asked:

```
#374:  TTY: setupCanAskAHuman(ui.tty, readerIsTerminal(in))   ← both ends
#401:  TTY: ui.tty                                            ← stdout only
```

`setupCanAskAHuman` and `readerIsTerminal` exist **only on #374**. Merging #401 first drops them, and setup would then prompt whenever *stdout* is a terminal while reading from a non-terminal stdin — the exact wedged-pipeline case `consent.go`'s own doc warns about. The two branches share 8 commits but neither contains the other, and both merge orders conflict on the second one.

So: **#374 first**, then reconcile #401 on top.

input.title: Fact locus extraction cuts file paths at hyphens and drops leading dots
input.description:
Reported by @ashtom in Slack.

A fact about `website/scripts/pre-build.ts` was anchored to `website/scripts/pre` and `build.ts` — two tokens that name nothing in the repo — while the real path never appeared. Re-recording the fact with the path in backticks did not help: the backtick span added the correct token, but the regex sweep still produced the fragments beside it.

## Root cause

One regex, `locusIdentifierPattern` in `internal/cli/facts_locus.go`. Two cuts of the same class:

1. **No `-` in any segment character class.** A segment ended at the first hyphen and the remainder restarted as a fresh token.
2. **No leading `.`**, and `factLocus`'s `add()` trimmed its punctuation cutset from *both* ends, so `.github/workflows/ci.yml` was stored as `github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Why a fragment is worse than a missing anchor

A fragment looks like a path, so it binds the fact to a file that does not exist — and `factLocusDrift` cannot flag it. `locusTokenIsFilePath` requires a slash **and** an extension: `website/scripts/pre` has no extension, `build.ts` has no slash, so neither reaches the `os.Stat`. A hyphenated file could be deleted and no fact about it would ever be reported as drifted.

The leading-dot case fails the opposite way: `github/workflows/ci.yml` *does* pass the file-path test and resolves nowhere, so it reads as drifted on every recall, forever.

## Fix

Segments become `[A-Za-z0-9_]+(?:-[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*` with an optional leading dot. The hyphen must be interior, so a trailing dash stays out of the token, and the first alternative still requires a `.` or `/`, which keeps ordinary hyphenated English ("state-of-the-art") out of the locus. `add()` trims leading and trailing punctuation with separate cutsets.

No migration needed: `reclassify` already rewrites `Locus` when it differs from what the text derives, so stored facts shed their fragments on the next pass.

## Verification

- Tests fail on main with exactly the reported symptom, backticked case included.
- Verified by weakening: dropping the interior-hyphen groups, the leading dot, or the asymmetric trim each turns them red; all three restored, green.
- Full `internal/cli` suite green; build and vet clean; 29 CI checks pass.

input.title: Ollama envelope test measured the fake server's own cap, not the client bound
input.description:
The ollama envelope guard was load-flaky and failed on `main`, not just on branches.

Root cause: the test's bound sat *inside* the fake server's own cap, so what it actually measured was scheduling, not the client's envelope limit. Under load the scheduler alone could push it over.

Fix: bound the guard by the client, not the writer, so the assertion is about the thing the test names.

content.text:
**#374 is merged.** #401's conflicts are resolved, pushed, and CI is on the last three macOS jobs. Summary while that finishes:

## What happened

You asked me to merge "the setup PRs" — that's **#374** (seven-phase UI, consent gate) and **#401** (short-form output). They couldn't just be merged in sequence.

**The catch I found first:** #401 sets the consent gate's TTY check to `ui.tty` — *stdout only*. #374 sets it to `setupCanAskAHuman(ui.tty, readerIsTerminal(in))` — **both ends**. Those helpers exist only on #374. Merging #401 first would have silently shipped a setup that prompts whenever stdout looks like a terminal while reading from a pipe that never EOFs. That's the wedged-CI case `consent.go`'s own doc warns about in capitals.

So: #374 first (clean), then reconcile #401.

## The four conflicts, and how each was decided

| file | kept | why |
|---|---|---|
| `.gitattributes` | **main's** | `*.golden*` is strictly broader than `**/testdata/*.golden*`, and I checked — no golden fixture lives outside a `testdata/` dir. Main's loses nothing. |
| `setup.go` | **#401's** | Main refreshes the push hook in a flat block after the watcher; #401 moved it into the AGENTS phase as `refreshSetupPushHook`, preserving all five branches. Taking main's would refresh twice — which main's *own comment* warns against. |
| `setup_render.go` | **#401's** | `renderSetupSummary` is the long renderer this PR replaces. Verified zero callers and no surviving reference to `summaryBarWidth` / `setupSummaryLabelWidth`. |
| `setup_render_test.go` | **#401's** | Same block's tests. |

Two things the merge couldn't resolve itself: `setup_render.go`'s `fmt`/`io`/`strings` imports were used only by the deleted renderer, and #374's `setup_consent_stdin_test.go` calls `newSetupSink(progress)` against #401's `(progress, quiet)` signature. I passed `quiet=false` so the gate still runs the full prompt path — a quiet sink could suppress the prompt and quietly stop exercising the read the test exists for.

## Verification

- **The fix survived**: `TTY: setupCanAskAHuman(ui.tty, readerIsTerminal(in))` is intact post-merge
- **Verified by weakening**: reverted it to `ui.tty` → `TestTheBackfillGateDoesNotBlockOnAPipeWithATerminalStdout` failed on the 20s clock with *"the consent gate read from a pipe that never EOFs"*. Restored → green.
- Full `internal/cli` **359s green**, `setupui` + `tui` green, build and vet clean
- Windows shards 0–7 all green on CI; macOS is the long pole (it runs ~17–20min against a 20min cap)

## Linear

## Three findings worth your attention

**#342 was shipping a dead flag.** Main replaced the remembered-decline path with the consent gate, and `setupConsentOverride` only knew `--no-backfill` and `--yes`. A user who declined once and then typed the documented way back in got **silence** — `--backfill` was read nowhere. Fixed.

**A cross-PR collision that was nobody's bug.** #398's test writes an "unknown" manifest field to prove the writer refuses it. It picked `suppressed_warnings` — which **#329 adds as a real field**, because disclosing what was dropped is its whole point. The test was asserting "unknown" about a name the product was still free to take. Repointed at a name no release will claim.

**Two tests were passing while checking nothing.** `TestWiringTheHookIsReportedAsDoneNotSkipped` searched for the word "skipped"; the renderer marks with a *glyph*, so it passed on every run. And #345's component-naming test searched the rendered block for `"sessions"` — which appears in the standing intro sentence. Both now assert against the function that owns the claim. I found these because the weakening didn't fire, not because they failed.

I also extracted two conditions (`setupAgentsPhaseDidWork`, `setupQueryabilityClause`) specifically because my first weakening attempts came back green — the code was correct but unreachable from any test. Rather than claim coverage I didn't have, I made them testable.

input.title: internal/cli has order-dependent tests that only fail under -shuffle=on
input.description:
Found while verifying the October merge stack. The suite is green in declaration order (local and CI), but `go test ./internal/cli/ -shuffle=on` fails reproducibly:

| run | failing |
|---|---|
| 1 | `TestDefaultEmbedderLoads`, `TestGlobalFactsNeverEnterARepositorysVectorCache`, `TestMCPRetrievalCanExcludeGlobalFactsPerRequest` |
| 2 | `TestHookSessionEndRecordsRecoveryHintAfterExportFailure` (+2 subtests) |
| 3 | same as run 2 |

These live in `embed_test.go`, `facts_global_test.go` and `hook_lifecycle_regression_test.go` — none of which the merge stack touched, so this is pre-existing, not a regression.

**Why it matters:** CI does not shuffle, so this is invisible there. It means some tests pass because an earlier test left process-global state behind (likely an embedder singleton and a vector-cache path). A test that passes for the wrong reason is the same class of problem as a test that asserts nothing — and it will surface as an unexplained CI failure the first time sharding or parallelism changes the order.

**Suggested fix:** run `-shuffle=on` in one CI job so the order dependence is caught where it is introduced, then isolate the offending globals (the embedder loader and the per-repo vector cache are the likely candidates).

Related: COR-2144 tracks a separate intermittent git-fixture `could not parse HEAD` failure in the same package.

**24 merged. 3 left.** Here's the plain-English version, Sun 11 Oct → now.

## What shipped

- **The brain's setup screen got cleaned up.** It used to dump a wall of text. Now it's five lines and a next step, with `--verbose` if you want everything back. That was your mockup feedback — it's live on main.
- **Fixed ashtom's bug.** The brain was chopping file names at hyphens: a memory about `pre-build.ts` got filed under `website/scripts/pre` and `build.ts`, two things that don't exist. Found a second version of the same bug with dot-folders (`.github/...` was stored as `github/...`). Both fixed.
- **Landed the entire-graph launch stack** — 40 pieces of work merged onto main across the week.
- **Cleared out the brain backlog: 24 pull requests merged today.** Setup, doctor, status, MCP, retrieval, the memory manifest, CI timeouts, the lot.
- **Closed two security questions.** The setup-go XML parser one (reachable but not exploitable; the actual finding was that none of our GitHub Actions are pinned) and the argv-parser one (only in benchmark tooling, never ships).

## Real problems found along the way

- **A flag that did nothing.** `--backfill` was supposed to let you undo an earlier "no, don't spend tokens". It was read nowhere — you'd type it and get silence.
- **Setup could hang.** It checked whether the *screen* was a terminal, then read from the *keyboard*. Piped into CI, it waited forever.
- **Two tests were passing while checking nothing.** One searched for the word "skipped" in output that uses a tick mark instead. The other searched for the word "sessions" — which appears in an ordinary sentence on screen, so it matched every time.
- **A message was 402 characters** in a box that fits 140, so it got cut off mid-sentence everywhere it appeared.
- **A function name was printed as a memory address** into a user-facing error. Tests didn't catch it; the Go vet tool did.
- **Two PRs quietly collided.** One used `suppressed_warnings` as a made-up "field that doesn't exist" in its test. The other added `suppressed_warnings` as a real field. Fine separately, broken together.

## Still open

- **#348** — one PR left. I was mid-fix when you stopped me; it's close but not finished.
- **#340** — nothing left in it (zero changes), just needs closing.
- **#350** — the old "combine everything" branch. Now redundant; it should be rebuilt as docs-only.
- **A stable release still isn't cut.** Anyone installing today gets a build from September. That's the last thing standing between you and P0 being done.
- ⚠️ **One hazard:** there are unpushed version tags (`v0.2.0`, `v0.3.0`, `v0.3.1`) sitting on this machine. A stray `git push --tags` would publish a release from whatever those point at.

## Linear

Four new issues filed for things that had no ticket: the locus bug (**COR-2180**), an ollama test flake (**COR-2181**), and tests that only fail when run in a random order (**COR-2183**). I haven't moved the ~17 existing issues to Done yet — that's next, now that their PRs are actually in.

Your git identity in `entire-brain` was set **repo-locally** to a placeholder:


entire.io attributes a session by its **first commit's author**. `r@r` maps to no GitHub account, so every session you ran in that repo came back unattributed — the server lists 50 recent sessions for `entire-brain` as **ashtom (23), evisdren (13), khaong (9), karthik (2), none (3)**, and not one as you.

| Session state files | 16 present ✓ |
| `entire/checkpoints/v1` | local and remote both `ea64fb41`, in sync ✓ |
| Pre-push hook | installed ✓ |

The work was captured, committed and uploaded the whole time. It was just signed by a name that doesn't exist.

**Fixed:** removed the local override, so the repo now inherits your real identity. Verified with a throwaway commit — new commits carry `Suhaan Thayyil <257360244+suhaanthayyil@users.noreply.github.com>`. Worktrees share the parent's config, so all 40+ got it at once.

**Only `entire-brain` was affected.** entire-graph, entire.io, entiredb and graphmark inherit the global identity; `cli` and `entire-api` set their own valid ones.

Both remotes point at the same URL here so nothing was lost — but on a repo where they differ, pushing to `origin` would leave checkpoints stranded. input.command:
git add -A && git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(watch,distill): stop the daemon racing its own worker, and stop paying twice for merged sessions

Three defects in the distill pipeline, all of which ship in the release.

COR-2175 — the daemon blocked itself.

The watch tick queued long-term reconciliation, launched `memory worker
--once` DETACHED, then ran a refresh needing the same brain write.lock. The
worker starts first and holds it 11-16s; refresh's timeout is shorter. The
tick logged brain_locked, skipped ALL agent work including distill, and did
not advance its cursor. 368 of 369 observed brain_locked failures followed a
reconciliation queued in the same tick, and any repo with an active session
has a changed transcript on nearly every tick -- so that repo's daemon distill
effectively never ran.

The watch tick now WAITS for the worker it spawned. Every other caller keeps
the detached launch: notify and the session-end hook are done once the work is
queued, and making them block on a 16s worker would slow a fast path for no
benefit. The wait costs a background tick the worker's runtime, which is the
right trade on a 5m interval -- a tick that takes 16s longer and then distills
beats one that returns fast having done nothing.

The issue offered "skip the worker and let refresh's consolidation do the
work" as the cheaper option. refresh.go contains no consolidation at all, so
that would have silently dropped it. Checked before choosing.

COR-2177 — distill re-paid for every branch copy.

The cache is keyed branch/session, and session export deliberately copies a
merged feature-branch session onto the default branch. Every copy was a cache
miss with zero chunk reuse, so the same transcript went back to the agent once
per branch. Measured on agent-insights: 69 "sessions" were 41 unique, 19 on
more than one branch, --dry-run reporting 209 of 209 chunks uncached.

Reuse is now content-addressed across every branch carrying the session, which
is sound because the hashes ARE content hashes: an identical chunk has already
been through the agent and its facts are already in the store, whichever branch
paid. Chunking is prefix-stable, so a copied transcript resolves almost
entirely from the union.

The matcher is segment-exact, deliberately. A substring match would let one
session's hashes mask another's, and a chunk wrongly believed distilled is a
chunk whose facts never get written -- worse than paying twice. Negative
controls cover "abc" vs "abcdef" and a branch named like a session.

COR-2176 — watch.log could not be read.

Bare `[watch] ...` lines, no clock, and on a workspace fan-out no way to tell
which repo a line was about. Diagnosing 2175 meant correlating two lines and
GUESSING they were the same tick on the same repo, which only worked because
one repo dominated that log. Stamped at the WRITER, so a line added later
cannot forget it, and per line rather than per write so a two-line tick does
not leave its second line unattributed.

Verified by weakening, four guards:
  - reverting the watch tick to the detached launch       -> red
  - removing the cross-branch half of the reuse decision  -> red
  - making the session matcher a substring                -> red
  - blanking the log stamp                                -> red

One of those only became a real guard after a correction: the first chunk-reuse
test asserted the helper directly and stayed GREEN when the call site was
changed to ignore it -- the same shape as the bug. The decision is now
distillChunksAlreadyDone, a value the loop calls, and the test drives that.

Full internal/cli suite green, every other package green, go vet ./... clean.

## COR-2175 — the daemon blocked itself 🔴

The watch tick queued long-term reconciliation, launched `memory worker --once` **detached**, then ran a refresh needing the same brain `write.lock`. The worker starts first and holds it 11–16s; refresh's timeout is shorter. The tick logged `brain_locked`, **skipped all agent work including distill**, and did not advance its cursor.

The watch tick now **waits** for the worker it spawned. Every other caller keeps the detached launch: notify and the session-end hook are done once the work is queued, and blocking them on a 16s worker would slow a fast path for nothing. The wait costs a background tick the worker's runtime — the right trade on a 5m interval.

> The issue offered a cheaper option: *"skip the worker and let refresh's consolidation do the work."* **`refresh.go` contains no consolidation at all**, so that would have silently dropped it. Checked before choosing.

## COR-2177 — distill re-paid for every branch copy 🔴

The cache is keyed `branch/session`, and session export **deliberately** copies a merged feature-branch session onto the default branch. Every copy was a cache miss with zero chunk reuse, so the same transcript went back to the agent once per branch.

Measured on `agent-insights`: 69 "sessions" were **41 unique**, 19 on more than one branch, `--dry-run` reporting **209 of 209 chunks uncached**.

Reuse is now content-addressed across every branch carrying the session. That's sound because the hashes *are* content hashes — an identical chunk has already been through the agent and its facts are already in the store, whichever branch paid. Chunking is prefix-stable, so a copied transcript resolves almost entirely from the union.

The matcher is **segment-exact**, deliberately. A substring match would let one session's hashes mask another's, and *a chunk wrongly believed distilled is a chunk whose facts never get written* — worse than paying twice. Negative controls cover `abc` vs `abcdef`, and a branch named like a session.

## COR-2176 — watch.log could not be read 🟡

Bare `[watch] …` lines: no clock, and on a workspace fan-out no way to tell which repo a line was about. Diagnosing 2175 meant correlating two lines and *guessing* they were the same tick on the same repo — which only worked because one repo dominated that log.

Stamped at the **writer**, so a line added later cannot forget it, and **per line** rather than per write so a two-line tick doesn't leave its second line unattributed.

Verified by weakening — four guards, each reverted individually:

| weakening | result |
|---|---|
| watch tick back to the detached launch | **red** |
| cross-branch half removed from the reuse decision | **red** |
| session matcher made a substring | **red** |

content.text:
**PR #426 is ready for tonight's release.** Checks passed, findings passed, up to date, mergeable. Only `Approvals` — yours.

## What's in it

**COR-2175 — the daemon was blocking itself.** The watch tick queued reconciliation, launched the memory worker detached, then ran a refresh needing the same `write.lock`. The worker always won; refresh timed out, logged `brain_locked`, **skipped all agent work including distill**, and didn't advance its cursor. 368 of 369 observed failures followed a reconciliation in the same tick — so on any repo with an active session, daemon distill effectively never ran. The tick now waits for the lock to clear.

**COR-2177 — distill paid twice for every merged session.** The cache is keyed `branch/session`, and export deliberately copies merged sessions onto the default branch, so every copy was a full cache miss. Reuse is now content-addressed across branches — sound because the hashes *are* content hashes.

**COR-2176 — `watch.log` was unreadable.** No clock, no repo. Stamped at the writer so a line added later can't forget it.

## Four mistakes I made, and how they surfaced

I want these visible rather than buried, because three were caught by CI and not by me:

1. **The first fix re-execed the test binary.** I waited on the *process* via `os.Executable()` — inside a test binary, that's the test binary, spawned and waited on. 36 tests stub `memoryWorkerLaunch` precisely to stop that; my new seam bypassed all of them. Now it waits on the **lock**, behind the seam they already stub.

2. **It then timed CI out at 30m42s.** My wait treated *every* lock error as "still held", so tests with unlockable brain dirs each sat through the full 90s budget. That failure was a **timeout, not an assertion** — I'd have misread it without checking the timestamps. Only `brain_locked` is waited out now; the suite is back to 322s.

3. **Two of my own tests were vacuous.** One measured elapsed time *after* joining the goroutine that released the lock, so it passed against a no-op. The other used a missing directory as its "unlockable" case — the lock just *creates* it and succeeds, so it passed against the exact bug it was written for. Both only showed up under weakening.

4. **A source-text guard failed twice on Windows shard 7** — first cwd, then CRLF, which my own notes already warn about. I proved the mechanism before fixing it the second time instead of guessing again.

Five weakening checks now hold: removing the settle call, making settle return immediately, dropping the contention filter, blanking the log stamp, removing the cross-branch half of the reuse decision.

## For tonight

Approve **#426**, then cut **COR-2157**. The stray tags are gone, so tagging is clean. **#350** should be closed or rebuilt docs-only — it exists to pre-integrate a stack that's already landed.

One caveat worth knowing before you tag: anyone who upgrades the brain before the `entire` CLI hits the `connect` failure I saw tonight — the brain calls `entire repo view --json`, which older CLIs reject. No ticket yet; say the word and I'll file it.

**Stop — do not merge this.** The review was right on all three decisive points, and I verified each myself.

## What's actually wrong

**1. COR-2177 is worse than the bug it fixes. 🔴**

Facts are stored **per branch** — `factsBranchRelDir(branch)` → `facts/<slug>-<sha>/facts.ndjson`, written by `writeFacts(brainDir, branch, …)`, never merged across branches. My comment claiming *"its facts are already in the store, whichever branch paid for it"* is **false**.

So: session distilled on `feature/x`, merged onto `main`, next run → my code marks every chunk already-done → extraction loop never runs → **zero facts land on `main`** → and the cache then records it as complete, permanently.

The bug I set out to fix cost money. My fix **loses memories**. That is precisely the failure mode my own code comment called "worse than paying twice", and I wrote it anyway.

**2. COR-2175 isn't fixed at all. 🟠** Measured it directly:

```
settle returned after 379µs   (worker takes the lock at ~50ms)
```

`launchDetachedSelf` returns at `command.Start()`; the child still has to boot Go, cobra, and two git calls before it touches the lock. My first poll fires microseconds later, finds the lock free, and returns. It only ever waits if the lock was *already* held.

**3. My test passed against that no-op** — it pre-holds the lock before calling settle, so it never exercises the launch→settle sequence that actually matters. I wrote a test for the shape I imagined instead of the one that occurs.

Also real, from the review: the key layout is `branch/discriminator/session`, so my `parts[1]` reads the *checkpoint id*, not the session (I confirmed at `distill_cmd.go:2440`); COR-2176 only wraps single-repo `runWatch`, not `runWorkspaceWatchPass` — the fan-out the rationale cites is still unstamped; and the settle can fire on `setup`'s path, where it could stall an interactive run.

## What I'd do about tonight

The honest read is that **COR-2177 can't ship tonight**. The ticket itself says the second half is *"decide how facts reach the second branch — carry or re-anchor the existing facts, in line with COR-2110"*. I implemented the first half and skipped the half that makes it safe. That's a design decision, not a patch.

My recommendation, and I'll start on your word:

- **Drop COR-2177 from #426.** Reopen it with these findings attached so the next attempt starts from the branch-partitioning constraint.
- **Fix COR-2175 properly** — settle must wait for the worker to *take* the lock, not merely find it free. A handshake (worker signals readiness) rather than a poll-and-hope.
- **Finish COR-2176** — wrap the workspace fan-out, which is the case that motivated it.

That keeps two real fixes in tonight's release and takes the dangerous one out.

https://entire.com/gh/entireio/entire-brain/trails/353
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

The supervised watch daemon (`entire-brain workspace watch --distill`, launchd `io.entire.brain-watch.*`) is the only automatic path that runs fact distillation, and on one machine it lost `locks/write.lock` on **576 of 724 ticks over 20 days**. A failed refresh skips the tick's agent work, so the 24h-gated distill ran **3 times in 20 days**.

## Root cause

| Fact | Value | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Brain write-lock timeout | 10s | `internal/cli/brain.go:33` (`brainWriteLockTimeout`), shared by ~375 `withBrainWriteLock` callers |
| Holder named in the timeout message | 12s to 25s old at the moment the waiter gave up (201 at 12s, 150 at 13s, 49 at 14s, ...); 21 ticks saw 1m4s to 15m37s | `~/.local/state/entire/logs/watch.log` |
| Who holds it | the detached `entire-brain memory worker --once` | `locks/write.lock.owner` and `locks/memory-worker.lock.owner` named the same pid (57068); the worker log shows that pass ran 10:07:23Z to 10:09:45Z |
| Who launched it | the same tick, one step earlier | `watchTick`: delta → reconcile (`reconcileMemoryAndLaunch` → `memoryWorkerLaunch`) → refresh |

The worker's prepass (`runRefreshDeltaStats` with export: `runExport` and `buildHistoryShortTermLockedContext`, both under write.lock) and its projection publish hold the lock for 12 to 25 seconds on this brain. The tick's heavy refresh asked for the same lock a second or two after launching that worker, waited 10s in session export ("session export degraded"), waited 10s again in seed baseline ("seed baseline failed", 652 ticks), and aborted the tick. The delta step, which runs *before* the launch, succeeded on 686 of those ticks, which is the tell that the tick was racing its own child.

Why every tick: the delta reports "14 transcripts failed to scan" on 652 ticks, so every tick is a repair tick (reconcile fires, worker launched, heavy refresh runs), and the repair backoff counter only advances on a successful refresh, so it never backed off while the refresh kept losing.

Not part of this: `dirty_worktree` (91 ticks) is the expected refusal while the tree has uncommitted edits (issue #327) and the tick already continues past it.

## Fix (watch.go only)

1. **Launch the worker after the refresh, not before.** The reconcile step is now a deferred closure with a ran-guard (same shape as `runFactsSync`), called explicitly after the refresh outcome on the main path. It still runs exactly once on every exit path (consolidation deferred, no change, refresh failed).
2. **Bounded retry on lock contention.** `watchRefreshWithLockRetry` re-attempts the free refresh only when the error is a lock timeout (`errFileLockTimeout` or the `brain_locked:` code), up to 3 retries with 15s / 30s / 60s waits, each capped at `--interval`, cancelled by ctx. 105s of waiting total, inside the 5-minute default interval. A 15s first wait outlasts the remainder of a hold that was already 12 to 25s old when the first attempt timed out. The global 10s timeout is deliberately unchanged: it serves interactive commands too.
3. **Pending gated work survives a lost lock.** If every attempt loses, and an earlier *successful* refresh (within one `--distill-every` window) left distill or seed pending, the tick runs it with the refresh cursor left where it was, so the next tick retries the refresh. This is the rule the no-change path already applies; it covers the minute-plus holders the retry cannot outwait.

## Tests

`go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'Watch'` is green, including nine new tests in `watch_test.go`: retry after a briefly held lock, bounded give-up with the 15/30/60s schedule, no retry for non-lock failures, ctx cancel during a wait, reconcile ordering on success / failure / deferred paths, pending distill running (and not running past the staleness bound) when the lock keeps being lost, the interval cap, and the error classifier.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Why 14 transcripts fail to scan on every tick: it turns every tick into a repair tick and launches a worker each time.
- The worker holds write.lock across its whole short-term build in the prepass. Shortening that hold would cut contention for hooks, the MCP server and `brief` as well.

## Problem

The distill cache salt hashed the agent, model and effort alongside the prompt, reconcile prompt and threshold. The facts are the product, not the model that produced them, so keying on the model meant the setup backfill (a resolved agent, effort low) and the session-end hook (auto, no effort) never shared a cache entry. Each re-spent on every session the other had already distilled.

On a real 289-session brain: a bare `entire brain distill --dry-run` reported **0 cached**, while `--agent codex --effort low` reported 72 of the same sessions. No facts had landed from the hook for 16 days.

## Change

- `distillCacheSalt` now covers only what the extractor was asked (prompt with taxonomy, reconcile prompt, confidence threshold) and the preprocessing version.
- Entries older binaries wrote under the agent-bearing formula are grandfathered against an enumerated set of known producer salts (the current run's own, plus codex and claude-code with and without effort low and a pinned model, in both preprocessing versions) and rewritten under the new salt on first sight. The hook migrates what the backfill wrote and vice versa; nobody has to repeat the writer's flags.
- The checkpoint fast path, the file-era-to-checkpoint content migration and the per-chunk reuse cache get the same grandfathering.
- The three salt derivations (current, legacy, legacy agent-bearing) share one prompt/threshold resolution.

## Tests

- `TestDistillCacheSaltIgnoresAgentModelEffort`: salt equality across agent, model, effort and agent command; prompt, reconcile, threshold and preprocessing version still invalidate.
- `TestDistillGrandfathersAgentSaltedCacheEntries`: seeded legacy entries cost zero agent calls on the backfill run, are rewritten under the new salt, cost zero calls on the hook's configuration, migrate under the hook's configuration too, and changed content still re-distills.
- `TestLegacyAgentDistillCacheSaltsEnumerateKnownProducers`, `TestDistillGrandfathersAgentSaltedCheckpointEntries` (identity entries and file-era content entries on a checkpoint-backed brain), `TestDistillChunkDoneUnderLegacySalt`.
- `TestDistillDryRunPredictsCacheAccurately` inverted: a different model now predicts all cached; a changed threshold predicts re-distill.
- `go test ./internal/cli/` passes.

## Verified on a real brain

Dry run with this build after one backfill pass: 147 cached under the default agent and under `--agent codex --effort low` alike. The pre-fix binary reports 0 cached for the same store under its default agent.

Three defects in the distill pipeline, all of which would ship in tonight's release. Closes **COR-2175**, **COR-2177**, **COR-2176**.

## COR-2175 — the daemon blocked itself 🔴

The watch tick queued long-term reconciliation, launched `memory worker --once` **detached**, then ran a refresh needing the same brain `write.lock`. The worker starts first and holds it 11–16s; refresh's timeout is shorter. The tick logged `brain_locked`, **skipped all agent work including distill**, and did not advance its cursor.

**368 of 369** observed `brain_locked` failures followed a reconciliation queued in the same tick. Any repo with an active session has a changed transcript on nearly every tick — so that repo's daemon distill effectively never ran.

The watch tick now **waits** for the worker it spawned. Every other caller keeps the detached launch: notify and the session-end hook are done once the work is queued, and blocking them on a 16s worker would slow a fast path for nothing. The wait costs a background tick the worker's runtime — the right trade on a 5m interval.

> The issue offered a cheaper option: *"skip the worker and let refresh's consolidation do the work."* **`refresh.go` contains no consolidation at all**, so that would have silently dropped it. Checked before choosing.

## COR-2177 — distill re-paid for every branch copy 🔴

The cache is keyed `branch/session`, and session export **deliberately** copies a merged feature-branch session onto the default branch. Every copy was a cache miss with zero chunk reuse, so the same transcript went back to the agent once per branch.

Measured on `agent-insights`: 69 "sessions" were **41 unique**, 19 on more than one branch, `--dry-run` reporting **209 of 209 chunks uncached**.

Reuse is now content-addressed across every branch carrying the session. That's sound because the hashes *are* content hashes — an identical chunk has already been through the agent and its facts are already in the store, whichever branch paid. Chunking is prefix-stable, so a copied transcript resolves almost entirely from the union.

The matcher is **segment-exact**, deliberately. A substring match would let one session's hashes mask another's, and *a chunk wrongly believed distilled is a chunk whose facts never get written* — worse than paying twice. Negative controls cover `abc` vs `abcdef`, and a branch named like a session.

## COR-2176 — watch.log could not be read 🟡

Bare `[watch] …` lines: no clock, and on a workspace fan-out no way to tell which repo a line was about. Diagnosing 2175 meant correlating two lines and *guessing* they were the same tick on the same repo — which only worked because one repo dominated that log.

Stamped at the **writer**, so a line added later cannot forget it, and **per line** rather than per write so a two-line tick doesn't leave its second line unattributed.

## Verification

Verified by weakening — four guards, each reverted individually:

| weakening | result |
|---|---|
| watch tick back to the detached launch | **red** |
| cross-branch half removed from the reuse decision | **red** |
| session matcher made a substring | **red** |
| log stamp blanked | **red** |

One only became a real guard after a correction: the first chunk-reuse test asserted the helper directly and stayed **green** when the call site was changed to ignore it — the same shape as the bug. The decision is now `distillChunksAlreadyDone`, a value the loop calls, and the test drives that.

Full `internal/cli` suite green, every other package green, `go vet ./...` clean.

- All CI is green. Entire Gates agent review found no blocking issues. I need an INDEPENDENT skeptical read before approving.

ALREADY RULED OUT (do not re-derive): the previous attempt at this bug (PR #426) tried to POLL the write lock after launching the worker; that is a measured no-op (settle returned in 379us while the worker takes the lock at ~50ms) because `launchDetachedSelf` returns at `command.Start()`. #442 does NOT do that.

  +package cli
  +
  +import (
  +	"bytes"
  +	"io"
  +	"time"
  +)
  +
  +// watchLogPrefixWriter stamps every watch line with the time and the repo it
  +// is about.
  +//
  +// watch.log is the only record of what a background daemon did, and it was
  +// written as bare `[watch] ...` lines: no clock, and on a workspace fan-out no
  +// way to tell which repo a line belonged to. Diagnosing COR-2175 meant
  +// correlating "reconciliation queued" with a "refresh failed" line further
  +// down and GUESSING they were the same tick on the same repo — which is only
  +// possible at all because one repo dominated that machine's log.
  +//
  +// The prefix is applied at the writer, not at the 26 call sites, so a line
  +// added later cannot forget it.
  +type watchLogPrefixWriter struct {
  +	out  io.Writer
  +	repo string
  +	now  func() time.Time
  +}
  +
  +func newWatchLogPrefixWriter(out io.Writer, repo string, now func() time.Time) io.Writer {
  +	if now == nil {
  +		now = time.Now
  +	}
  +	return &watchLogPrefixWriter{out: out, repo: repo, now: now}
  +}
  +
  +func (w *watchLogPrefixWriter) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
  +	// Split on newlines so a multi-line write gets one stamp per line rather
  +	// than one for the batch. The trailing empty element of a newline-
  +	// terminated write is skipped, so no bare prefix is emitted.
  +	lines := bytes.Split(p, []byte("\n"))
  +	var buf bytes.Buffer
  +	stamp := w.now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)
  +	for i, line := range lines {
  +		if i == len(lines)-1 && len(line) == 0 {
  +			buf.WriteByte('\n')
  +			break
  +		}
  +		if i > 0 {
  +			buf.WriteByte('\n')
  +		}
  +		buf.WriteString(stamp)
  +		if w.repo != "" {
  +			buf.WriteString(" " + w.repo)
  +		}
  +		buf.WriteByte(' ')
  +		buf.Write(line)
  +	}
  +	if _, err := w.out.Write(buf.Bytes()); err != nil {
  +		return 0, err
  +	}
  +	// Report the caller's length: the prefix is ours, not theirs, and a short
  +	// count makes io.Copy and friends think the write failed.
  +	return len(p), nil
  +}

fix(watch): attribute every daemon log line with its clock and repo

watch.log is the only record of what a background daemon did, and it was
written as bare `[watch] ...` lines: no timestamp, and on a workspace
fan-out no way to tell which repo a line was about. Diagnosing the
write.lock race (COR-2175) meant correlating a "reconciliation queued"
line with a "refresh failed" line further down and guessing they were the
same tick on the same repo, which only worked because one repo dominated
that machine's log.

The stamp is applied at the writer rather than at the ~30 call sites, so
a line added later cannot forget it, and per line rather than per write,
so a two-line write does not leave its second line unattributed.

Attribution is decided by the LOOP, not the tick, in both paths:
watchLoop wraps its own sink with the repo key, and workspaceWatchLoop
hands each member an already-stamped writer. A tick only writes to what
it is given. Each sink is wrapped exactly once; the single-repo banner is
stamped beside the loop rather than inside it, so nothing nests.

Workspace-level lines carry the clock alone: they belong to no one repo.

Verified by weakening, six guards, each reverted individually:

  watchLoop stops wrapping                      -> red
  workspace loop hands the tick a raw writer    -> red
  writer omits the repo key                     -> red
  writer stamps per write instead of per line   -> red
  mid-line continuation tracking removed        -> red
  Write reports its own length, not the caller's -> red

Closes COR-2176.
